content.content:
CLOSED fix/prune-leaf-expansion-and-pinned-units — fix: expand pruned roots to their leaves and plan reclaim in pinned bytes
---
Prune drops old file versions and reclaims their bytes. Prune is a **write-plane mutation** — it re-seals and publishes a shortened history — which is why #820 pulled it into this chain. Slice settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813.

## Scope

**This issue absorbs #849, #850 and #851 outright.** They were previously named as prerequisites in prose only, with no dependency edge, which made #872 look startable when it is not — and made three defects look like three shippable PRs. They are not: `plan_prune` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:93`) has **zero production callers** at `main` @ `3d087d673`. Its only references are the re-exports at `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:54` and `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:38`, and its own unit tests in `retention.rs`. Nothing reaches it, so none of the three is independently observable or independently testable end-to-end. Close all three as folded-in when this ships. Native `blocked_by` edges are recorded on this issue so the graph stays honest until they are.

**Three correctness fixes, folded in.**

- **#849 — leaf expansion.** `plan_prune` emits root content CIDs only, and `POST /registry/retire` deletes rows for exactly the CIDs handed to it without walking the DAG, so every sealed leaf stays pinned and charged forever while `reclaimed_bytes` reports the whole version freed. Expand each doomed root to `root + leaf_cids` before retiring, by fetching the root block and `decode_root`-ing it — the root block is plaintext det-CBOR, so no key is needed. Two constraints on its shape: `root + leaf_cids` **cannot be one call** — the registry batch cap is `REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX = 1000` (`crates/engine/src/net/mod.rs:25`), enforced by the chunking at `crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs:100`, and a 1 GiB version is 1025 targets at the frozen 1 MiB framing, so partial retire is normal at exactly `max_file_bytes` — and **leaves retire before their root**.
- **#850 — unit mismatch.** `ContentVersion.size_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:75`) is documented as the **pinned** size, but the prune path fills it from `Version.size`, which is **plaintext** bytes. The gap is fixed and computable (40 B per sealed leaf, plus the root block). A pending-reclaim total built on the wrong unit is the same misreport in a new place. Derive the pinned total from the leaf count and root size rather than reusing the plaintext number.
- **#851 — partially already fixed; check before you write.** The ticket claimed `keep_latest` admits zero at `retention.rs:72-73`. That is stale in two ways. `RetentionPolicy::KeepLatest(NonZeroU64)` **already exists** (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:65`), with the doc stating the zero state is unrepresentable rather than guarded. The hole survives only on the free function: `plan_prune(versions_newest_first: &[ContentVersion], keep_latest: usize)` at `retention.rs:93` still takes a plain `usize` and `skip(0)` still yields the whole history including the live version. Close that one signature; do not re-do the enum.

**One op that ends at publish, plus a retire ledger that is not an op** (#852). Both alternatives put a garbage-collection call on the critical path of user work: one op with two legs holds the FIFO head so the next rename waits on cleanup, and two ops repeats that plus a sixth `OpKind` with vacuous rebase semantics.

**The ledger stores roots; leaves are re-derived** at drain time via `decode_root` — plaintext det-CBOR, no key. That is three orders of magnitude smaller, and it is the irrecoverable half: once the publish lands nothing readable references the dropped roots, while leaves always can be recovered from a root.

## #1026 audit — it cannot close yet

PR #1101 landed most of it. Residual filed 2026-08-07 as six new issues, all parented under #635:

- **#1135** grant tags bound to the retired root name (the security one, see below)
- **#1136** scope pointer never renews, lapses at its 90-day EOL
- **#1137** 2 of 3 re-point channels return `NotLanded` — no wire shape exists for either
- **#1138** `root_retire_ready()` hard-coded `false`, migration-window constant does not exist
- **#1139** nothing ever mints a `write_history_link`, so a resumed wave cannot recover its seed
- **#1140** no test holds the read-epoch floors still across a whole wave

Edges: #1019 blocked_by #1135/#1136/#1137/#1139; #1127 and #1016 blocked_by #1135; #764 blocked_by
#1139. **#1026 still needs the ADR 0004 `Status:` flip on cipher-box-next before it closes** — that
stays a checkbox on #1026, not an issue.

Unfiled, needs a decision: `publish_moved` publishes `content_cids: Vec::new()`, so after a wave
every node's pins stay accounted to its retired name. #1125 covers register-vs-retire but not the
name-move case.

## The defect: a moved root name orphans every grant tag

`kdf::blinded_tag` binds the scope root `ipnsName`, and a write rotation moves that name by
construction. `reseal_root` rewrites `commitment.ipns_name` and owner-re-signs, but clones
`commitment.entries` and passes `grant_ledger` verbatim, so blobs stay filed under dead tags.
`classify` reads "fresh owner-signed record, no blob at my tag" as the **definitive** revocation
signal ahead of every epoch check — so one write revoke reads as a mass read-revoke, unrecoverable
client-side (`RepointObject.prev_root` carries one hop).

Survived because **every wave fixture commits an empty grant set**. The blind spot is structural:
`RepublishedNode` deliberately carries no owner material, so the pure `rotate_scope_write`
simulation can never reach this class. Same family as the wave-6 "trust an unsigned field" class in
[[project-wave6-closed]].

**#1127 must sequence behind #1135**, not beside it: #1127's check refuses a row whose
`recipientEncPk` does not re-derive its tag, which on the write-wave path fires on every *honest*

What is misplaced is the *policy*: "a download ticket dies when its transfer ends" is a property of that ticket, and this PR expresses it as a promise the caller must remember to await, a deadline the web app must calibrate against a Service Worker constant it cannot see, and a bound that holds only because one `for` loop happens to `await`.

### 1. `packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:126` + `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileDownload.ts:66-79` — the ticket's lifetime policy is exported as a caller obligation instead of a ticket property

`whenIdle`/`whenStreamIdle`/`await`/`revoke` is a four-step protocol every future minting site must reassemble correctly, and nothing enforces it. The download path wants one thing: *a ticket that dies when its transfer ends*. The preview path (`apps/web/src/hooks/useFilePreview.ts:58-63`) wants the opposite and correctly scopes the ticket to the component — so the two lifetimes are a real distinction, and it belongs at the mint site.

**Deeper fix:** put the lifetime on the ticket — `createStreamUrl(source, { oneShot: true })` (or `lifetime: 'transfer' | 'held'`), with the registry/broker auto-revoking once the ticket's last cursor drops (or the stall deadline passes without one ever appearing). The waiter, the timer, and the stall constant all become broker internals; `useFileDownload` mints and forgets; the promise on `save()` survives only if it is still wanted for the spinner, derived from the same signal rather than being the mechanism.

### 2. `packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:139-144` — `expire()` resolves a waiter without ever consulting the pin it is supposed to be tracking

This is the one place the new machinery *should* meet the existing pin lifecycle and doesn't. `bump()` is called from exactly two sites — `acquire()` (broker.ts:196) and post-chunk (broker.ts:412) — and both imply `cursors > 0`, i.e. states the deadline should not be able to fire in at all. But a body **between pulls** has no deadline anywhere in the system: `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:56` and `:68-73` say so explicitly ("a body between pulls has none", "a buffered media element may go a long time without pulling again"). So a save whose body is open but not pulling for 45 s — the browser blocked on a Save-As dialog is the obvious case — expires the waiter, and `useFileDownload.ts:76` then revokes a *live* transfer, which `revoke()` turns into `'the stream was revoked'` on the body.

That also makes the comment at `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileDownload.ts:22-27` ("A stalled read fails at the pipe's own pull deadline well before this, so it only ever catches a save the browser never began") false: the pipe's 30 s pull deadline only exists *while a pull is in flight*.

**Deeper fix:** the deadline exists to catch "no body ever claimed this ticket" and "the reader vanished without saying so". Make it say that: on expiry, if `this.pins.get(ticket)` still has `cursors > 0`, the reader is registered — re-arm (or defer to a separate, much longer phantom-cursor watchdog) rather than declaring idle. With that, `bump()` at broker.ts:196 and :412 collapses entirely, because progress is only interesting where no cursor is registered.

Nothing in the registry caps live tickets.

# Security review — `fix/775-cold-seed-anchor-role-from-scope-identity`

No modifications made. Verdict: **the change is a net security improvement; no directly exploitable vulnerability found.** Three latent issues.

## 1. MED — Decoded `scopeId` is authenticated but not bound to the AAD scope
`crates/core/src/payload/pointer.rs:170,206` · `crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs:345`

`open_pointer_payload` builds the AAD from the **caller's** `scope_id` (`pointer_ctx(v, *scope_id)`), then returns `RepointObject::from_value` **without cross-checking the decoded `scopeId` against it**. The diff makes a trust branch (run vs skip the revocation-floor check) depend on that unchecked field.

Not currently exploitable: `seal_pointer_payload:150` always derives the AAD from `object.scope_id`, so any block that opens under scope X necessarily decodes to X. The invariant is real but **implicit — enforced only by the encoder**, in a codebase whose own rule (AGENTS.md §8) demands both sides enforce it. `seal_repoint` (`sync/pointer.rs:161`) takes the key and the object as *separate* arguments, so a future caller can pass the root pointer read key with a foreign-scope object and mint the mismatch. Consequence if it ever exists: the vault anchor classifies `Shared`, the revocation-floor check is skipped, and `cold_seed:314` seeds floors under `repoint.scope_id` while the adoption gate reads them under `root_scope_id` (`net/adopter.rs:254`) — the vault's revocation floor is never seeded and a rolled-back re-point is adopted silently.

**Fix:** in `open_pointer_payload`, after decode, reject `object.scope_id != *scope_id` as a `TrustViolation`. One line, makes the mismatch unrepresentable.

## 2. LOW — Root scope ids are the constant `[0u8;16]` for every user
`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1570,1669` (`root = NodeId([0u8;16])`, `root_scope_id = root.0`)

`AnchorRole::for_scope` (`gate/floor.rs:143`) assumes scope ids are globally distinguishing. They are not at the root. If a user's **root** scope is ever shared, the grantee's cold-seed of it compares `[0;16] == [0;16]` → misclassified `Root` → the read-epoch false-positive the `Shared` role exists to avoid, and the two scopes collide on one floor key (read-epoch floor is keyed by the bare scope id, `floor.rs:176`), poisoning the local vault's own revocation floor. Latent only: `cold_seed_checked` has exactly one production caller (`sync/boot.rs:213`); no shared-scope cold-seed exists.

**Fix:** derive a per-vault root scope id rather than the constant, or key floors by `(scope_id, owner)`. Track before the shared-scope cold-seed lands.

## 3. INFO — Clean on the remaining focus areas
- **Q2 (root → `Shared` bypass):** not reachable. The only mismatch source is finding 1.
- **Fail-closed ordering:** correct — both checks precede any write; the write-epoch check stays unconditional for every role; `cold_seed` still runs for `Shared` (covered by `cold_seed_checked_shared_scope_seeds_a_fresh_read_epoch_floor`).
- **Determinism:** no clock or RNG introduced; role selection is a pure comparison.
- **API surface:** the role is no longer nameable by any caller — the wiring-level bypass #775 targeted is genuinely closed.</result>

<result>## Verdict

The refactor is directionally right and mostly correct, but it has **one fail-open bug on a required check**, a **small wall-clock regression on the longest CI chain**, and the **caching premise it's built on is largely inert in this repo**. Details, worst first.

---

### 1. `Web Bundle` is now silently green when the WASM build fails — HIGH

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml:245-251`**

`Web Bundle` is a *required status check* (confirmed via the branch-protection API: contexts include `"Web Bundle"`, but **not** `"Web Engine WASM"`). It now carries `needs: [changes, lint, wasm-engine]` with `if: !failure() && !cancelled() && web == 'true'`. When `wasm-engine` fails, `failure()` is true → `web-bundle` is **skipped** → GitHub reports the required `Web Bundle` context as skipped, which branch protection counts as passing.

The author spotted exactly this hole for `web-e2e` and patched it into `web-e2e-result` (ci.yml:894-914) — but `Web Bundle` is required *by name*, so no result gate covers it. Before this diff `Web Bundle` built the WASM itself and went red.

Cost: a broken engine build merges with a green `Web Bundle`. Fix at the right altitude: add `Web Engine WASM` to the required contexts. It's a stable job name that always reports, a failure goes red, and a skip counts green — which also makes the `web-e2e-result` loop below unnecessary.

### 2. Critical-path regression on the longest chain — MEDIUM

**`ci.yml:876-878`** (`web-e2e` gains `needs: wasm-engine`)

Measured from run `31181193884` (a clean, cache-cold PR run):

| | before | after (est.) |
|---|---|---|
| `Web E2E Smoke` chain | lint 26s + 243s = **269s** | lint 26s + wasm-engine ~160s + web-e2e ~105s = **~291s** |
| `Web Bundle` chain | lint 26s + 179s = **205s** | lint 26s + ~160s + ~70s = **~256s** |

## 1. Fail-closed / false-green — **one MED, otherwise clean**

**MED-1 — `Web Bundle` is a required context that now fails *open* on a `wasm-engine` failure.**
`ci.yml:245-253`. Branch protection (verified via `repos/FSM1/cipher-box/branches/main/protection`) requires the literal context `Web Bundle`, and there is no `Web Bundle Result` aggregate. `web-bundle` now has `needs: [changes, lint, wasm-engine]` with `if: !failure() && ...`, so a `wasm-engine` failure **skips** `Web Bundle`, and GitHub scores a skipped required context as passing.

The merge is still blocked today, because `Web E2E Smoke Result` is also required and the diff correctly extended it to cover `wasm-engine`. But two things are now true that weren't:

- The dependency is invisible from the required-context list.

*Fix:* add a `web-bundle-result` always-reporting gate over `[wasm-engine, web-bundle]` mirroring `contract-suite-result`, and swap the required context from `Web Bundle` to `Web Bundle Result`.

**Verified clean:**
- `wasm-engine`'s `if` (`web || e2e`) is a superset of `web-bundle`'s (`web`) and identical to `web-e2e`'s — there is no case where a consumer runs without its producer.

### 2. MEDIUM — a failed first settings save locks the device out of all content writes, with no wired recovery path

`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:452` (mint raise) → `:664-677` (verdict) → `:279` (refusal) → `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2433-2436`

**Mechanism.** `next_revision` persists the mint raise at settings.rs:452, before the PUT. Everything after it can fail without a record ever reaching the network: `encode_settings_body` (:494), entropy fill / all-zero guard (:497, :502), `seal_settings_record` (:508), `preflight_settings` (:511), `publish_record` (:513), and `Unconfirmed` (:546). Each leaves the mint counter raised on a device that holds no sequence floor. The next cold start hits :664, finds no record, reads a raised mint, and returns `Suppressed`.

**Blast radius is a whole session, not one write.** The placement decision is computed once at facade.rs:1654 and never recomputed — the only other writes to `self.placement` clear it (facade.rs:1699 on cold-start failure, :1772 on shutdown). **Who can trigger it.** Not remotely. `publish_settings` is only reachable from a member-initiated save; grepping the tree, the only callers are tests, and the lib re-export at `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:92`. Nothing in `facade.rs` or `crates/wasm` invokes it. A network adversary can *cause* the save to fail, but only after the member initiates one. An ordinary offline or flaky-network first save does it just as well.

**Recoverable in principle, not in practice on this tree.** One successful `publish_settings` clears it: :553 writes last-known-good, :554 raises the bare-name floor, and the record lands, after which loads resolve or degrade to `Stale`. There is also no offline escape: a save cannot land while offline, and every failed attempt re-raises the mint.

- Narrow the window. The revision value must be known before `encode_settings_body`, but the *durable raise* need not be. <result>## Crypto/privacy review — `fix/703-revival-corroborates-recovered-sequence`

Report only; no files touched.

### 1. [MEDIUM] Revival enforces the sequence floor but never the read-epoch floor

`crates/engine/src/net/revival.rs:105-116` compares only `sequence_floor`. `crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs:166-201` (`check`) is the floor law's pair: sequence **and** read-epoch (the revocation boundary, `epoch < epoch_floor` → fail-closed).

Mechanism: `basis.sequence < floor` is a strict `<`, so a basis at exactly the durable floor passes with **any** value. Device A durably adopted seq 5 (epoch 1); device B rotated at seq 6 (epoch 2); after a >EOL lapse seq 6 is gone from every endpoint. `fanout_get_verify` + `recovery_fetch` both yield seq 5, basis passes (5 < 5 is false), and `revival.rs:116-123` re-mints the **pre-rotation, pre-revocation** CID at seq 6, superseding the rotation cut. Gated readers then reject the new head on the epoch stage — a revocation rollback that degrades into a fail-closed lockout at that name.

Fix: at `revival.rs:109`, require identity at the floor, not just non-regression — persist the adopted head value alongside the sequence floor and demand `basis.value == adopted_head` when `basis.sequence == floor`; or thread `scope_id` in and run the basis envelope through the adoption gate before it becomes the re-mint head.

### 2. [LOW-MEDIUM] Module doc contradicts the code — a single endpoint *is* still the sole basis

`revival.rs:12-15` claims "one endpoint's word is never the basis on its own". `revival.rs:97-100`: when `fanout_get_verify` returns `None` (every routing endpoint censored, offline, or serving nothing), `basis = recovered` — the untrusted recovery endpoint alone. Also `revival.rs:82-85` hard-fails on `recovery_fetch` **before** the fan-out runs, so the API can unilaterally veto revival even when the routing set holds a good record. Fix: reword to the true property ("the freshest of the two sources"), and make `Recovery(_)` fall through to a fan-out-only basis rather than aborting.

### 3. [LOW] `unwrap_or(0)` silently disarms the guard on a never-adopted name

### Structural

1. **`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abd827e5eeed25d4e/crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:203`, `:487`, `:526`, `:533` — the same `Pending { .. }` literal written four times.**

   Simpler: `impl Pending { fn new(len: u64, base: Base) -> Self { Self { spill: None, len, base, dirty: false } } }` — the four sites become `Pending::new(0, Base::Empty)` / `Pending::new(len, Base::Version)`.

2. **`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:522-541` — `truncate_handle` re-implements `begin_pending`.**
   The `else` arm (`len: self.base_len(handle, open.node).await?, base: Base::Version`) is `begin_pending` verbatim, wrapped in its own `contains_key` guard that `begin_pending` already performs. The `size == 0` arm's `len: 0` and `base: Base::Empty` are then both overwritten unconditionally by lines 546-549, so the whole if/else exists only to *skip* the `base_len` resolve when truncating to zero.
   Simpler — same behavior, ~15 lines gone:
   ```rust
   if size == 0 {
       self.pending.entry(handle).or_insert_with(|| Pending::new(0, Base::Empty));
   } else {
       self.begin_pending(handle, open.node).await?;
   }
   ```
   with lines 542-551 unchanged.

3. **`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:656-673` — `spill_mut` does three `HashMap` lookups and two unreachable `ok_or(BadHandle)`s to lazily fill one `Option`.**

   Simpler:
   ```rust
   let block_bytes = self.cache.block_bytes();
   let area = &mut self.spill;
   let pending = self.pending.get_mut(&handle).ok_or(VfsError::BadHandle)?;
   if pending.spill.is_none() {
       pending.spill = Some(area.create(block_bytes)?);
   }
   pending.spill.as_mut().ok_or(VfsError::BadHandle)
   ```

4. **`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:629-653` — `version_block` looks `pending` up twice, and `Pending::block` (`:81-89`) is a single-use two-line delegation.**
   `base` is `Copy`; read it in the same borrow as the spill probe, then inline the `match`:
   ```rust
   let pending = self.pending.get_mut(&handle).ok_or(VfsError::BadHandle)?;
   let base = pending.base;
   if let Some(spill) = pending.spill.as_mut()
       && let Some(block) = spill.block(index)? { return Ok(block); }
   ```
   One lookup, one `BadHandle`, and the `impl Pending` block plus its doc comment disappear.

5. **`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:382-400`, `:590-598`, `:610-622` — three copies of the same block-framing arithmetic.**
   `index = cursor / block_bytes; within = cursor - index * block_bytes; take = min(...)` appears in `write`, `push_version`, and `read_pending` with only the per-block action differing (and a fourth, cache-aware variant in `read` at `:325`).    Simpler: one private `fn frame(offset: u64, end: u64, block_bytes: u64) -> impl Iterator<Item = (u64 /*index*/, usize /*within*/, usize /*take*/)>` and let the three loops be `for (index, within, take) in frame(..)`. `read` keeps its own loop (it needs the short-block EOF break).

6. **`crates/fuse/src/spill.rs:136-149` — `truncate` splits one retain predicate into a retain plus a special-case `remove`.**
   `retain(|i| *i <= last)` followed by `if within == 0 { remove(&last); return }` is exactly "keep blocks whose start offset is below `len`".
   Simpler, one predicate and one early return:
   ```rust
   let block_bytes = self.block_bytes;
   self.blocks.retain(|index| index.saturating_mul(block_bytes) < len);
   let within = (len % block_bytes) as usize;
   if within == 0 { return Ok(()); }
   let last = len / block_bytes;
   ```

8. **`crates/fuse/src/spill.rs:56-58` — `std::process::id()` in the spill filename buys nothing.**
   `SpillArea::open` deletes every file in the dir, so a second process over the same dir destroys the first's spills regardless of naming; within one process `minted` is already unique, and `create_new(true)` is the backstop. `format!("spill.{}", self.minted)` is the same guarantee.

# Security Review — `fix/703-revival-corroborates-recovered-sequence`

Scoped to this PR's own diff (`crates/engine/src/net/revival.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/net.rs`). The `gate/floor.rs`, `sync/boot.rs`, `tests/sync.rs` hunks belong to the parent `#775` branch and were excluded per instruction.

## Vuln 1: Tie at equal sequence resolves in favor of the untrusted recovery endpoint — `crates/engine/src/net/revival.rs:97-100`

- **Severity: LOW** (confidence 7)
- **Category:** `trust_boundary` / content rollback
- **Mechanism:** the guard is strict `>`. At `observed.sequence == recovered.sequence` the `_ =>` arm keeps `recovered` — the copy from the endpoint this PR's own commit message names as the compromised source. Same-sequence forks are not exotic here: `publish.rs:93-96,326-335` documents that an `Unconfirmed` publish is retried *at the same sequence*, so two validly-signed records with different `Value`s at one sequence are a designed-for state. The attacker picks which of two owner-authored CIDs is re-minted.
- **Bound:** both candidates are Ed25519-signed by the name's key, so this is CID selection among owner-authored states, not injection.
- **Fix:** prefer the fan-out record on `>=`, or return an explicit fork verdict when sequences tie and bytes differ.

## Vuln 2: Corroboration degrades silently to zero sources; absent floor defaults to 0 — `crates/engine/src/net/revival.rs:97,108`

- **Severity: MEDIUM** (confidence 8) — residual, not a regression
- **Category:** `replay` / fail-open-on-unavailability
- **Mechanism:** `fanout_get_verify` swallows every per-endpoint transport error as `continue` (`fanout.rs:105`) and returns `None`, which is indistinguishable from "no endpoint has the name". `revive` then falls back to the single recovery record. `unwrap_or(0)` at `revival.rs:108` makes the floor check inert whenever the device has no durable floor for the name (first revival on a fresh device, or post floor-store reset). 1. **No injection.** `IpnsName::public_key` (`name.rs:96-99`) returns the key parsed from the name's own multihash — canonical-form-enforced at `name.rs:68-94`, no `pubKey` side channel. `record.rs:163-185` verifies `signatureV2` against it and returns the sequence *and* value from the same signed `data` blob (`signed.value != top_value` rejects). ## Why

**1. The central security claim — "truncate(2) reports success on a failed commit" — is factually wrong.**

`ops.rs:426-431`:

```rust
let Some(handle) = handle else {
    let handle = self.handles.open(node, Access::Write);
    let truncated = self.truncate_handle(handle, size).await;
    let released = self.release(handle).await;
    return truncated.and(released);
};
```

`Result::and` is `Ok(_).and(res) == res`, `Err(e).and(_) == Err(e)`. `release` (`:457-465`) returns `committed` — the `commit` result — as its own return value, and `commit` (`:556-580`) propagates every failure from `begin_write`/`push_version`/`commit_write`. So when the truncate stages fine but the commit fails, the expression evaluates to `Err(commit error)`. The no-handle truncate path **cannot** return `Ok` on a failed commit. There is no false ack of destruction, and a SETATTR adapter would relay that as an errno to userspace. The finding's own escalation hook (shred primitive silently no-op'ing) does not exist.

Note also that truncate is not a shred/erasure primitive in this system regardless: content is immutable content-addressed sealed data, a truncate publishes a new version rather than destroying the old bytes, and no security control depends on it having happened.

**2. `close(2)` is covered by `flush`, not `release`.** `flush` (`:444-446`) and `fsync` (`:451-453`) both call `commit` and return its error — which is exactly the POSIX/FUSE contract (`close(2)` returns FLUSH's status; the kernel structurally discards RELEASE's, by protocol design, for every FUSE filesystem). The genuine residual is a narrow reliability gap, not a vulnerability.** The only case where a commit failure has no userspace-visible channel is mmap writeback dirtying pages after the last FLUSH — a scenario that requires the durable staging store to be failing, is not attacker-influenced, has no trust-boundary or fail-open dimension, and is common to essentially every FUSE filesystem. It is a durability/reliability defect at worst.

**4. Also relevant to weighing it:** `crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs` is only the invalidation trait (131 lines) — no kernel protocol binding exists on this branch, so the "the RELEASE reply value is discarded by the kernel" step of the argument is about a layer this PR does not contain; the core's caller receives the `Result` either way.

Retaining spills after a failed commit would *increase* ciphertext-at-rest lifetime. Reporting it as a security finding is inverted.</result>

**B7 done — two independent draft PRs, both two files, both `MERGEABLE`.**

**[#1145](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1145) — #1037, zeroize the upload chunk.** The issue turned on ownership, and the agent settled it rather than guessing: the chunk reaches `EngineHost.pushChunk` by transfer at every hop (`transport.ts:135`, and the follower's `broadcastTransport` → `leaderRelay` chain), so it is detached in the sender's realm and the worker is the terminal owner. `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:289` takes `chunk: Vec<u8>`, so wasm-bindgen marshals into linear memory before `push_chunk` returns its promise — the wipe cannot race the copy. One private `scrubbing` helper wipes in a `finally`, so the reject path scrubs too. The tests assert the WASM side saw real bytes, so a wipe that fires too early cannot pass.

**[#1150](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1150) — #1051, fail closed in `buildCommand`.** Every field of all 16 command kinds now passes an `unknown`-taking checker. Beyond the ask, it fixed `nodeKind`/`permission`, which fell through to `Folder`/**`Write`** on an unrecognised literal — the same coercion class one layer down, and a silent privilege upgrade. The `never`-bound default was verified by temporarily adding a 17th kind and confirming `tsc` rejects it.

Gates green on both from the committed tree, and full CI settled with zero non-success checks.

**Two out-of-scope defects filed.** #1154 (blocked by #1051): `beginWrite`/`snapshot`/`download`/`openContentStream` read the same untrusted message with the same coercion, and it is sharper there — `passArray8ToWasm0` is `Uint8Array.set(arrayLike)`, so a 16-character *string* reaches `NodeId::from_bytes` as sixteen zero bytes and passes the Rust length check, producing a request against the wrong node instead of a refusal. #1155 (blocked by #1037): `EngineClient.pushChunk` and `CorrelatedTransport.request` drop a refused chunk before any transfer, so it is never detached and never wiped, while `EngineClient.start` and `LeaderRelay` already scrub on their equivalents.

Both arrived orphaned again — parented under #993, `comp:web`, milestone v2.0.0. Their dependency edges were correct. That is three follow-up issues from two batches filed with only `v2-build`; I will fold the parent/label/milestone requirement into the shared brief so later waves do not repeat it.

One process note worth keeping: the #1051 branch was accidentally cut from the #1037 branch, because `git checkout main` fails in a worktree when main is checked out elsewhere. The agent caught it by checking `gh pr view --json files` against the expected file count, then rebased `--onto d11bfce11` and re-ran every gate. Six batches still running.

`gate::floor::cold_seed_checked` took `AnchorRole` as an argument, so a future shared-scope caller could have selected it from a `RepointObject` field and suppressed the read-epoch regression check at the vault anchor. The role is no longer an input at all — it is derived from the re-point's own `scope_id` against the session's root scope id, both trusted. The `AnchorRole` enum was deleted outright (review found it became dead public surface once nothing could pass it).

Files: `crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs`, `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/sync.rs`.

**The recorded #1141 rebase check was a no-op in practice**: the new caller stayed in `gate/floor.rs` + `sync/boot.rs`, so it touched no `mint_grant_row` call and constructed no `ScopeRootIdentity`. No conflict with #1141, confirmed by a clean `cargo test --workspace` on top of `d11bfce11`.

**A production `AnchorRole::Shared` caller could not be wired, and this is a real tracker gap.** The grantee-plane shared-scope resolve does not exist: `scope_pointer_name` derives the pointer name from the *owner's* `ownerPointerSeed`, which a grantee never holds, and no wire field carries that name to a grantee. `open_repoint` has no non-test caller, `grants::accept` persists a `pointerReadKey` nothing reads back, and `Command::AcceptShare` returns `Unimplemented`. Deterministic, no race, reachable from ordinary unprivileged `ftruncate(2)`. `create` correctly sets `Base::Empty` (`ops.rs:207`), so this affects exactly the pre-existing-file case where deleted content exists.

**[#1148](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1148) — #775.** `cold_seed_checked` took `AnchorRole` as an argument, so a future shared-scope caller could have selected it from a `RepointObject` field and suppressed the read-epoch regression check at the vault anchor. **A real tracker gap surfaced.** A production `AnchorRole::Shared` caller cannot be wired, because the grantee-plane shared-scope resolve does not exist: `scope_pointer_name` derives the pointer name from the owner's `ownerPointerSeed`, which a grantee never holds, and no wire field carries that name to a grantee. `open_repoint` has no non-test caller, `grants::accept` persists a `pointerReadKey` nothing reads back, and `Command::AcceptShare` returns `Unimplemented`. **[#1157](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1157) — #703**, based on #1148's branch. `revive` trusted a single `recovery_fetch` record as its CAS basis; the routing fan-out now corroborates it, the head CID is read from the same record as the sequence, and a basis below the durable floor fails closed as `StaleSource`. Residuals filed as #1161 — parented and labelled, its edge to #703 was already right.

**#856 returned as analysis, not a rushed change**, and I agree with the call. The diagnosis holds, and design B — an account-namespacing `FloorStore` decorator — is right, because every downstream consumer is already generic over `F: FloorStore`, so the whole cost is about ten call sites in `facade.rs`. ## 1. Non-zero `ftruncate` resurrects deleted plaintext into the published version

`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:517-552` — **Severity: MEDIUM**, confidence 9/10. Confirmed.

**Mechanism.** `truncate_handle` records a shrink as only `pending.len = size`. It sets `pending.base = Base::Empty` only when `size == 0` (`ops.rs:547-549`), and `SpillFile::truncate` (`spill.rs:136-149`) only retains/zero-tails blocks the spill *already holds* — on a freshly opened handle the spill is empty, so it is a no-op. `Pending` (`ops.rs:70-79`) carries no truncation floor. Later, `version_block` (`ops.rs:642-652`) resolves any block the spill does not hold by reading the pinned **pre-truncate** base version via `engine.read_stream`, which knows nothing of `pending.len`. `push_version` (`ops.rs:592-598`) then walks `0..len` with no clamp and publishes those bytes.

**Repro — two syscalls, no write needed.** File has a published 100-byte version. `open(O_RDWR)`; `ftruncate(fd, 10)` → `Pending { spill: None, len: 10, base: Version, dirty: true }`; `ftruncate(fd, 100)` → spill is `None` so the spill truncate is a no-op, `len = 100`, `base` stays `Version`; `close(fd)` → every block falls through to the base stream and the published version is byte-for-byte the original 100 bytes. The shrink is entirely undone. The shrink-then-write-past-the-cut variant yields the same for the gap region, which POSIX requires to read as zeros.

**Why security-relevant.** The resurrected plaintext is re-sealed and published as a new *live* version, so (a) a file shared after the user truncated sensitive bytes away exposes those bytes to a recipient who never held the prior version, and (b) the deleted tail is carried into every later version and into a rotated epoch's reseal. Deterministic, no race, reachable from unprivileged `ftruncate(2)`. `create` correctly sets `Base::Empty` (`ops.rs:207`), so this hits exactly the pre-existing-file case where deleted content exists.

**Fix.** Add a truncation floor to `Pending` (e.g. `zeroed_from: Option<u64>`, set on every shrink, raised/cleared as writes fill it). Have `version_block` return zeros — never a base read — for indices wholly at or past the floor, and zero the tail of the straddling block after the base read.

**Test gap.** `crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs` exercises truncate only at `size == 0` (lines 986, 1068, 1094, 1115) — the one case `Base::Empty` masks. Add shrink-then-grow and shrink-then-write-past tests.

`crates/fuse/src/spill.rs:38-46` and `spill.rs:225-229` — candidate severity LOW. **I could not confirm this**: its validation agent never returned, so I have no verdict on it. Correcting an earlier statement of mine in this session that called it filtered — that was premature and wrong.

No nonce is ever reused under a key. Key is `Zeroizing`, memory-only, never logged. All new plaintext buffers are `Zeroizing`. `spill_io` errors carry only `io::ErrorKind`, never a path or content byte. # Wave 7 — common brief for every batch agent

Base: `main` @ `d11bfce11`. Repo `FSM1/cipher-box`.

## Read first

1. `AGENTS.md` (root) — project law. Read all of it.
2. `CONTEXT.md` — the v2 ubiquitous language. Use these terms exactly.
3. The `blueprint/*.md` that covers your crate (`core`, `engine`, `api`, `web-client`, `desktop`, `testing`).
4. Your issue body: `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N> --jq .body`.
   The bodies are long and cite exact `file:line`. Some cites are stale — re-check every one against the tree.

**Mandatory recon:** branch `v1` often holds a reference implementation of the same behaviour.
Check it (`git show v1:<path>`, `git log v1 --oneline -- <path>`) before designing anything new.
This has overturned issue scopes before.

## File ownership — the hard rule of this wave

Each batch OWNS a file set. **Never edit a file another batch owns.** If your issue seems to need
one, stop, do everything else, and say so in your report. Do not "just make a small edit" there.

| Batch | Issues | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | 1016 | `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, `crates/wasm/src/host.rs`, `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/facade.rs` |
| B2 | 1110 | `crates/fuse/**`, `crates/desktop-seams/src/paths.rs`, `crates/desktop-seams/src/fs_util.rs` |
| B3 | 872 | `crates/engine/src/content/**`, `crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs`, `crates/engine/src/net/mod.rs`, `crates/engine/src/seams/retire_ledger.rs`, `crates/engine/src/seams/mod.rs`, `crates/engine/src/sync/op.rs`, `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`, `crates/contract/**` |
| B4 | 775, 703, 856 | `crates/engine/src/gate/floor.rs`, `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs`, `crates/engine/src/net/revival.rs`, `crates/engine/src/seams/floor_store.rs`, `crates/desktop-seams/src/floor_store.rs` |
| B5 | 1084 | `crates/engine/src/settings.rs`, `crates/engine/src/sync/pointer.rs` |
| B6 | 1088 | `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**` |
| B7 | 1037, 1051 | `packages/client/src/worker/**` |
| B8 | 1126, 1064 | `apps/web/src/hooks/**`, `apps/web/src/components/**`, `packages/client/src/media/**`, `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts` |

Shared and unavoidable: `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` is a re-export barrel. Keep your edit there to
**purely additive re-export lines** so a merge conflict stays trivial. Same for `crates/engine/src/error.rs`
if it exists in your path.

`crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` is shared by B3 and B5 — both append test functions only, never
restructure the file.

## Worktree and build hygiene

- You run in your own git worktree. **Do not set or share `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`** — a shared target dir
  across worktrees serves stale test binaries and produces identical-looking passes.
- For any TypeScript work, run `pnpm install` inside your worktree. **Never symlink `node_modules`**
  from the main checkout.
- Use the scratchpad path given in your own task prompt. It is unique to you. Do not write to a
  sibling's path.

## Gates — run these before you open the PR

**zsh has no `PIPESTATUS`.** Never pipe a gate through `tail`/`head` and read `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` — it
comes back empty and you will report a false pass. Redirect to a file, read `$?` directly, then read
the file.

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                  ; echo "fmt=$?"
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   > /tmp/clippy.log 2>&1 ; echo "clippy=$?"
cargo test --workspace                      > /tmp/test.log 2>&1 ; echo "test=$?"
cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown > /tmp/wasm.log 2>&1 ; echo "wasm=$?"
```

- `cargo fmt --all` — never scope it to `-p`; the CI gate is workspace-wide.
- `--workspace` never builds `wasm32`. The wasm check is a separate required gate; run it whenever you
  touch `crates/engine`, `crates/core`, or `crates/wasm`.

TypeScript work adds: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`.
Rebuild a package's `dist` before typechecking a consumer of it.

Every gate must be green, from the **committed** tree, before the PR opens. Report the real exit codes.

## Code law you must follow

- All crypto and codec logic is Rust in `crates/core` / `crates/engine`. TypeScript never implements crypto.
- Prefer TypeScript string-literal unions over `enum`.
- Determinism is injected: entropy, time, and policy arrive as parameters or seam traits. Never call a
  clock or an RNG directly in core/engine logic.
- **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry** (AGENTS.md rule 8): where a decode path hard-rejects an
  invariant, the matching encode path must enforce it with a **release-active** check returning `Err` —
  never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`. Cover it with a test that fires in release.
- Zeroize at the terminal owner only. A callee must never zero a caller-owned buffer.
- Comments say **why**, briefly. No absence-justifying comments (prose defending a path that is not in
  the code). No apologia for a workaround — fix the code instead. No unchanged-code apologia.
- **No tracker references in code comments.** A bare `#1234` fails the `Tracker Refs` gate. State the
  checkable condition instead ("the real wiring is not landed"). Citations of the frozen decision corpus
  (`FSM1/cipher-box-next#32`, or a bare one/two-digit `#NN`) are exempt.
- Assert behaviour, never source text. Every new suite must be covered by a named CI gate.
- Markdown edits: MD036 forbids a `**bold**` line used as a heading; MD031/MD032 require blank lines
  around fences and lists.

After the draft PR is open, run each of these on your own diff (`git diff main...HEAD`):

1. `/simplify` — remove speculative generality, dead abstraction, duplication.
2. `/security-review` — trust boundaries, fail-closed behaviour, auth/expiry gates, injection,
   resource exhaustion, concurrency, determinism seams.
3. `/crypto-privacy-review` — **required if the diff touches crypto**: `crates/core` primitives, key or
   seal material, or a trust-boundary/fail-closed read.

If a slash command is unavailable, do a rigorous manual pass against that checklist instead. Never skip
a gate. Fold real findings back into the code and tests, and re-run the gates after.

Verify the mechanism yourself; a literal application has twice produced a worse bug.

- **Never push to `main`.** Branch as `feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `chore/`, `test/`, `ci/`.
- Conventional Commits for every commit: `type(scope): description`. **No parentheses anywhere in the
  subject line** — a custom commitlint rule rejects them and they break Release Please.
- Always prefix gh with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Open the PR **as a draft** and leave it draft. Do not mark it ready. Do not merge it.
- PR body: end with `Closes #<your issue>`. Use `Part of #<umbrella>` only for a genuine umbrella.
- **No Claude or AI attribution anywhere in the PR body or title.**
- In the PR body, escape any `#NN` that is not a real issue reference so GitHub does not autolink it.
- Opening a PR can trigger a bot release commit — `git fetch` and rebase before your next push.
- If commit signing hangs, do not pass `--no-gpg-sign`; guard the command with `timeout` and retry.

## Report back

Return a compact report: branch, PR number and URL, issue closed, files touched, the four gate exit
codes, what each review gate found and how you resolved it, and anything you had to leave undone
because it lived in another batch's files.

Two review-sub-agent failure modes hit in one wave (wave 7, 2026-08-07). Brief every reviewer you
spawn with both, explicitly, in the spawn prompt.

**1. A review sub-agent ran `git checkout --` on its parent's working tree and destroyed three
in-flight edits.** It mistook a sibling batch's concurrent work for a rogue agent and "cleaned up".
The parent recovered, but only because it noticed. Ban all git writes for reviewers — `checkout`,
`reset`, `stash`, `commit`, `push`, `clean`. Reviewers read; they do not write. This is sharper when
many worktree agents run at once, because a reviewer sees unfamiliar concurrent activity and
misreads it as corruption.

**2. A reviewer reported a candidate as "filtered out as a false positive" while its filter agent was
still running**, then self-corrected on the next turn. A missing verdict is not a negative verdict.
Require reviewers to carry an unvalidated finding forward as **unvalidated**, never as confirmed or
dismissed.

**Why:** both fail toward a false all-clear — the same family as the wave-4 review-cycle defect
classes in [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]]. The first also destroys work silently.

**How to apply:** put both rules in the shared wave brief that every batch agent reads, and require
each batch to pass them down when it spawns its own reviewers. See
[[project-wave7-planning-state]] for the brief pattern — one scratchpad file read by every agent,
carrying ownership, gates, and review rules, instead of repeating the constraints per prompt.

## Problem

A partial write over a file whose current version has an **unprojected size** is refused, and there is no path that clears the refusal except waiting for a publish.

`crates/fuse` assembles a new version block by block from three sources: the per-handle spill, the base version, and hole-zeros. To read a block from the base it must know the base version's size. An unprojected size is **unknown, not zero** — guessing zero would silently drop the file's tail into the published version — so the write path fails closed instead.

The engine's read plane resolves **published heads only**. So a file whose `updateContent` is staged in the op queue but not yet published has no resolvable size, and any partial write over it is refused until the publish lands.

## Why it matters

The refusal is correct — failing closed is the only safe choice when the base length is unknown, and #1110's crypto-privacy review already showed what the alternative costs. It found a HIGH defect of exactly this family: a shrink that recorded no floor on the base version re-served bytes a member had truncated away and re-sealed them into the next published version.

But the refusal is user-visible in an ordinary case. Appending to a file that was just written is a normal editor and shell pattern, and the window is however long the op queue takes to drain and publish. The user has no signal that waiting is the remedy.

## Scope

This is an engine-side limitation and cannot be fixed from `crates/fuse`. Two directions, either of which closes it:

- Let the read plane resolve the size of a version that is staged but not yet published, so the base length is known before the publish lands.
- Or carry the staged version's length on the op itself, so a consumer can learn the base length without resolving a head.

Whichever lands, the invariant `crates/fuse` depends on must hold: a base length is either **known** or the write is **refused**. A defaulted or guessed length reintroduces the truncation-resurrection defect.

## Acceptance

- A partial write over a file whose latest `updateContent` is staged but unpublished succeeds, and the published version contains the correct tail.
- No path supplies a defaulted base length. An unknown length still refuses.
- A test covers append-over-staged-version end to end, not only the unit refusal.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`.

---

Found during #1110, PR #1156.

**B6 done — [#1147](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1147)**, draft, closes #1088. All 30 checks pass.

The wasm engine now builds once per run as an artifact, `Web Bundle` carries no Rust toolchain at all, and two composite actions collapse the `wasm-bindgen-cli` install across five jobs and four workflows — where the staging copy had already drifted.

**Both review passes independently found the same HIGH, and it is fixed.** `Web Bundle` is a required context *by name*, so a producer failure would have **skipped** it, and branch protection scores a skip as a pass. Gating the consumers on `lint` instead of `!failure()` fixes it — and a run accidentally proved it end to end: the producer failed and `Web Bundle` went red on `Artifact not found` rather than silently passing. That is the same fail-toward-a-false-all-clear family as the desktop matrix deadlock. Also fixed: the CLI version check was a `grep -qw` regex that an empty version would satisfy against any binary.

**The agent reported an honest miss rather than claiming the gate.** Runner minutes on the web chain drop 31% cold, 422s → 293s, and the proc-macro fix is proven — a PR touching one engine file recompiled 63 crates in 37s before, 3 crates in 13s after. But the issue's *wall-clock* target is not met on a cold cache: +46s. The cause was measured, not guessed — 104s of the cold producer job is `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli` from source, which used to run twice in parallel and now runs once on the critical path.

The fix for that is #1152, and it is **blocked on a decision only you can make**: the agent implemented the prebuilt-binary install and had to revert it, because the repo's Actions allowlist rejects `taiki-e/*`. Allowing it would take the producer 158s → about 54s cold and close the gap. #1153 is separate and worth knowing regardless — `ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only and caches are scoped to the writing ref, so **every PR's first run is cache-cold on every cargo job**. Verified: 39 cache entries, exactly one on `refs/heads/main`. Both were filed orphaned again; parented under #995 with `comp:ci` and the milestone.

Two other things need you rather than an agent. `Web Engine WASM` should be added to required contexts — it is path-filtered, so it reports `skipped` and satisfies protection on non-web PRs. And `desktop-e2e.yml` still holds a third divergent copy of the mock-routing boot; the agent left it deliberately, because it is a three-OS dispatch-gated matrix that no PR gate would have exercised, and said so in the PR body instead of converting it blind. I think that was the right call.

One batch left: B3 on prune.

## Problem

`Engine::command` now answers with a `CommandOutcome`, and the `ImportContact` arm answers with the imported `Contact` itself. Nothing in TypeScript can read it.

The WASM `command()` promise changed from resolving `bigint | undefined` to resolving a `CommandOutcome` object. No TypeScript change shipped with it. The whole surface typechecks only because the sole consumer discards the result: `packages/client/src/worker/engineHost.ts:106` does `await this.handle.command(buildCommand(...))` and returns `void`.

So the `contactImported` outcome and the two public keys it carries are unreachable from a host today. A contact can be imported, and the caller cannot learn what it imported.

## Why it matters

`Contact` has no public constructor, so holding one is the proof that its binding verified. Discarding it throws away exactly the evidence the fail-closed import was built to produce. A host that wants to show the user which peer they just added has no way to ask.

This also hides the ordinary case behind a shape that already changed. A later reader sees `command()` returning an outcome and reasonably assumes the import path is live end to end. It is not.

## Scope

- Read the outcome in `packages/client/src/worker/engineHost.ts` instead of discarding it, and carry it back over the worker boundary.
- Surface `identityPublicKey` and `encPublicKey` from the returned value. The WASM boundary hands back an exported class, so the caller must call `.free()` once it has read the fields.
- Keep the queued case working: `CommandOutcome::op_id()` is what the event-correlation path reads, and it must keep flowing.

## Acceptance

- A host calling the import command receives the imported contact's two public keys.
- The queued-operation path still correlates by `opId`, with no behaviour change.
- The boundary object is freed after its fields are read, with a test that fails if it leaks.

## Gate

`Test`, `Typecheck`.

content.text:
**Wave 7 is fully launched and merge-verified. The result is better than I expected.**

**No branch needs a code fix before it merges.** The cumulative compile check invented zero fixes — every shape change was already absorbed on its own branch. The full eleven-branch merge runs `cargo test --workspace` at 1644 tests passing and `pnpm test` at 837, with wasm32 and `fmt` green.

The three shape-change risks I was worried about all turned out to be non-issues, for checkable reasons: the only FUSE call site discards `command()`'s result, so widening its return type is source-compatible; B1 added the `MalformedInput` arm to the exhaustive `From<EngineError>` impl itself; and nothing outside B4's own branch still referenced the deleted `AnchorRole`.

**File ownership was the right axis.** Across 55 pairs there are two conflicts, both predicted by the batches, both keep-both edits in test files. `write_plane.rs` is about 60 lines of append reassembly — git mis-aligns the shared four-line test preamble as common context and interleaves the hunks — and `FileBrowserActions.test.tsx` is about ten. Each belongs to whichever of its pair merges second.

**Safe merge order:** #1147 → #1151 → #1157 → #1156 → #1149 → #1158 → #1145/#1150/#1146 → #1160. One trap in that list: **#1157 contains #1148**, so never merge #1148 separately afterwards. #1158 owns the `write_plane.rs` resolve and #1160 owns the `.tsx` one.

**One real gap came out of the verification** and is now #1167: the WASM `command()` promise changed from `bigint | undefined` to a `CommandOutcome`, but no TypeScript shipped with it, and it typechecks only because `engineHost.ts:106` discards the result. So the imported contact and its two public keys are unreachable from a host. `Contact` has no public constructor, so discarding it throws away precisely the evidence the fail-closed import exists to produce.

**Three things are yours, not an agent's.** Whether to allow `taiki-e/*` in the Actions allowlist, which closes #1152 and the last cold-cache wall-clock gap. Whether to add `Web Engine WASM` to the required contexts. And #1156 — the FUSE write path handles plaintext at rest, and its `/security-review` was self-performed because the skill agent died twice, so I would put an independent pass on it before it goes ready.

Ten follow-up issues were filed across the wave. Every one arrived orphaned with only `v2-build`; all are now parented, component-labelled, milestoned and edged. I have added that requirement, the no-git-writes rule for review sub-agents, and the cumulative-merge compile check to the shared brief and to memory so the next wave starts from them.

**Three pairs are the same subsystem, same author, same review lens, and should be one PR each.** Consolidating them takes you 11 → 8:

1. **#1148 + #1157** → one PR, +354/−86, 5 files. #1157 is *already* stacked on #1148, so today it costs two review slots for what a reviewer reads as one chain anyway.
2. **#1145 + #1150** → one PR, +210/−34, 4 files. Both are fail-closed hardening inside `packages/client/src/worker/**`. Neither is big enough to justify its own slot.
3. **#1146 + #1160** → one PR, +796/−31, 20 files. This is the one with a second payoff: these two **conflict with each other** in `FileBrowserActions.test.tsx`, so combining them deletes that conflict rather than deferring it to whoever merges second.

The other five stay alone and I would not merge them: #1151 is the shape change everything rebases onto, #1156 and #1158 are 1352 and 1770 lines in security-sensitive paths, #1147 is CI-only, #1149 is its own trust decision.

**Two things also reduce the pain without touching the PRs.** The 1-per-hour limit is CodeRabbit's, org-wide, and it fires automatically when a PR goes ready — so the lever is *when you flip each one to ready*, staged in merge order, not how many exist. Greptile has no such cap and will review all of them regardless. And the three mandatory gates already ran on every PR with real findings folded in, so CodeRabbit here is the additional layer, not the floor.

Want me to do the three consolidations? It is rewriting three branches and closing three PRs — none merged, so nothing is lost, but it is my hand on your open PRs, so I would rather you say go. **Consolidated: 11 → 8 PRs.** All three merges verified before I touched GitHub, and nothing is lost — no branch was deleted.

| PR | Size | Now covers |
|---|---|---|
| #1147 | +169/−124, 6f | #1088 CI |
| #1151 | +373/−53, 9f | facade shape + `ImportContact` |
| #1157 | +354/−86, 5f | **#775 + #703** |
| #1156 | +1352/−41, 10f | #1110 FUSE write |
| #1149 | +327/−63, 4f | #1084 settings |
| #1158 | +1770/−98, 25f | #872 prune |
| #1145 | +210/−34, 4f | **#1037 + #1051** |
| #1146 | +796/−31, 16f | **#1126 + #1064** |

**#1157 needed no git rewriting at all** — it was already stacked on #1148, so its tip was a strict superset. Retargeting its base to `main` and closing #1148 was the whole job. That stack was costing you two review slots for what a reviewer reads as one chain.

**#1146 absorbing #1160 deleted a conflict rather than deferring it.** Those two were the pair that clashed in `FileBrowserActions.test.tsx`; I resolved it keep-both, and confirmed `service.ts` carries both `onStreamError` at :89 and `whenStreamIdle` at :124, with the web suite at 257 tests — matching the independent merge check exactly, so neither side was silently clobbered.

Both rewritten branches pass `pnpm install`, `typecheck`, `test`, `lint` and `lint:tracker-refs` from the committed tree. I re-scanned every remaining pair afterwards: **one conflict left**, `write_plane.rs` between #1149 and #1158. That one is inherent — different subsystems appending tests to the same file — so consolidating them would mean merging settings work into the prune PR, which is worse than a 60-line append-both resolve.

**Merge order:**

1. **#1147** — CI only, touches nothing else, merge whenever
2. **#1151** — the `command()` shape change; land it early so the rest rebase onto it
3. **#1157** — floor and revival
4. **#1156** — FUSE write path
5. **#1149** — settings
6. **#1158** — prune; **owns the `write_plane.rs` resolve**, about 60 lines of append-both
7. **#1145** — worker
8. **#1146** — media

Items 7 and 8 are independent of the Rust chain and can go in parallel with any of it.

Two things still worth doing before the queue starts: give **#1156** an independent security pass, since it handles plaintext at rest and its `/security-review` was self-performed after the skill agent died twice. And since CodeRabbit fires automatically on ready-flip at one per hour org-wide, flip them to ready in the order above rather than all at once, so the review capacity is spent in merge order.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
3	# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
4	# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
5	#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
6	PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
7	cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
8	GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"
9	
10	# The head is the key every later check keys on, so a transient failure here must
11	# abort rather than proceed with an empty string that silently matches nothing.
12	HEAD=""
13	for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
14	  HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha' 2>/dev/null)
15	  case "$HEAD" in [0-9a-f]*) [ ${#HEAD} -eq 40 ] && break ;; esac
16	  HEAD=""; echo "  head read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
17	done
18	[ -n "$HEAD" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ HEAD FOR #$PR - aborting, nothing flipped."; exit 7; }
19	echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"
20	
21	# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
22	#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
23	#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
24	MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
25	# SKIPCI=1 during an Actions outage: CI can never go green, and a CodeRabbit slot
26	# expires whether or not it is used, so waiting for CI throws the slot away.
27	[ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && echo "SKIPCI=1 - not gating on CI (Actions outage)"
28	for i in $(seq 1 30); do
29	  [ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && break
30	  sleep 20
31	  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
32	  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
33	  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
34	  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
35	  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
36	  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
37	    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
38	    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
39	    exit 4
40	  fi
41	  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
42	    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
43	  fi
44	  sleep 40
45	done
46	
47	# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
48	NOW=$(date -u +%s)
49	if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
50	  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
51	fi
52	
53	BASE=""
54	for a in 1 2 3; do
55	  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
56	  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
57	  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
58	done
59	[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
60	echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"
61	
62	# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
63	# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
64	# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
65	FLIPPED=0
66	for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
67	  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
68	  sleep 5
69	  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
70	  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
71	  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
72	  sleep 20
73	done
74	[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }
75	
76	# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
77	#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
78	#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
79	CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0; MS_REVIEWED=0
80	for i in $(seq 1 40); do
81	  sleep 60
82	  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
83	  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
84	    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
85	    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
86	    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

# The head is the key every later check keys on, so a transient failure here must
# abort rather than proceed with an empty string that silently matches nothing.
HEAD=""
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$HEAD" in [0-9a-f]*) [ ${#HEAD} -eq 40 ] && break ;; esac
  HEAD=""; echo "  head read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$HEAD" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ HEAD FOR #$PR - aborting, nothing flipped."; exit 7; }
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
# SKIPCI=1 during an Actions outage: CI can never go green, and a CodeRabbit slot
# expires whether or not it is used, so waiting for CI throws the slot away.
[ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && echo "SKIPCI=1 - not gating on CI (Actions outage)"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  [ "${SKIPCI:-0}" = "1" ] && break
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=""
for a in 1 2 3; do
  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
FLIPPED=0
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
  sleep 20
done
[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0; MS_REVIEWED=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$U_NOW" ] && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    # "completed" is not "reviewed": a skipped run completes too. Out of credits,
    # macroscope skips all five with "Credit balance exhausted", which the old
    # completed-count test scored as full coverage.
    MSR=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.conclusion!="skipped")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSX=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select((.output.title // "")|test("[Cc]redit balance exhausted"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$MSX" ] && [ "$MSX" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      MS_DONE=1; MS_REVIEWED=0
      echo "  MACROSCOPE OUT OF CREDITS on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED, not waiting"
    elif [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ]; then
      MS_DONE=1
      if { [ -n "$MSR" ] && [ "$MSR" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
        MS_REVIEWED=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE REVIEWED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ($MSR of $MST agents ran)"
      else
        MS_REVIEWED=0; echo "  MACROSCOPE ALL SKIPPED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED"
      fi
    fi
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

# Re-draft must be confirmed too: a PR left ready collects an unplanned review.
for a in 1 2 3 4; do
  $GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$D" = "true" ] && { echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; }
  echo "  re-draft attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"; sleep 15
  [ "$a" = "4" ] && echo "WARNING: #$PR MAY STILL BE READY - re-draft it by hand"
done

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -iE "actionable comments posted|nitpick comments|no actionable comments" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
echo "-- coverage --"
echo "coderabbit_reviewed=$CR_DONE macroscope_reviewed=$MS_REVIEWED"
[ "$MS_REVIEWED" = "1" ] || echo "WARNING: macroscope did NOT review this head. CodeRabbit is the only bot verdict."
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

content.text:
Decisive check: **#1113 merged with `Web Bundle: SKIPPED`**, and `Web Bundle` is already a required context. So GitHub does treat a skipped required check as satisfying protection here, and `Web Engine WASM` uses the same `needs: [changes, lint]` + `if:` pattern. The change is safe.

**Yes, I will handle it — but not immediately after the merge, and this is worth a moment.** A required context blocks any PR whose head never reports it. All seven queued PRs are based on `d11bfce11`, which has no `wasm-engine` job at all, so the moment I add that context they would every one go unmergeable until rebased — seven rebases and seven full CI runs, purely as a side effect of a settings change.

So I recommend adding it **after the wave lands**, not after #1147. I will do it then, verify it against a real PR rather than assuming, and tell you if the write is refused for permissions — I can read branch protection, but I have not tested whether I can PATCH it.

Worth noting the producer already fails safely without it: B6 changed `Web Bundle` to gate on `needs.lint.result == 'success'`, and proved empirically that a failed producer now turns `Web Bundle` red on "Artifact not found" instead of skipping it into a false pass. Making `Web Engine WASM` required is belt-and-braces on top of that, not the thing holding the gate shut.

Understood on the reviewers — CodeRabbit only for this batch, Greptile back mid-August, macroscope pending the OSS programme. I will drop the independent-reviewer suggestion and not raise it again. Recording that so it does not get re-proposed in a later session.

Diagnosed. CodeRabbit is not rate-limited and it did start — its status comment updated at 16:22:31Z, one minute after the flip, and it names the correct head range `d11bfce11...2e1696e3c` and all 8 files, with run ID `3756a9ff`. But it has been sitting on **"Currently processing new changes in this PR. This may take a few minutes, please wait..."** for 38 minutes. That is CodeRabbit being slow or stuck on their side, not a queue or limit problem.

The script's poll window expires about now, so it will re-draft and exit `INCOMPLETE`. That is the correct outcome and it does not lose the review — re-drafting does not cancel an in-flight CodeRabbit run, so the verdict will still land on that head when it finishes. I am not re-flipping, which would burn a second slot for a review already in progress.

Setting a separate watch for the late verdict.

**The short answer: CodeRabbit started fine and then stalled on their end.**

What the evidence says:

- It picked up the job one minute after the flip — status comment updated 16:22:31Z, run ID `3756a9ff`.
- It is reviewing the right thing: commit range `d11bfce11...2e1696e3c`, 8 files, `Cargo.lock` correctly excluded by the path filter.
- **No rate-limit message anywhere** — zero comments matching "Review limit reached", so the slot was genuinely spent and accepted.
- The comment still reads "Currently processing new changes in this PR. This may take a few minutes, please wait…" 38 minutes later.

So this is not a queue problem, not a limit problem, and not the script failing to detect a verdict. It is CodeRabbit taking far longer than its own estimate. For contrast, #1147 went from flip to clean verdict in three minutes.

The script's 40-minute window has now expired, so it re-drafted #1151 and exited `INCOMPLETE`. That is the right behaviour — and the review is not lost, because re-drafting does not cancel an in-flight run. I deliberately did **not** re-flip, which would spend a second hour's slot on a review that is already running.

I have a separate watch on #1151 looking for the verdict to land late, distinguishing three outcomes: a review with findings on that exact head, a clean verdict once "Currently processing" clears, or a rate-limit message appearing.

The next slot opens around **17:21Z**. If #1151's verdict has landed by then I will start #1157 as planned. If CodeRabbit is still stuck, I would rather not feed it another PR while it is degraded — I will tell you what I see and let you call it.

Cost is the reason. Keep that in mind before suggesting anything that burns review credits.

## Do not re-review after a nitpick-only fix

**Confirmed by the user 2026-08-07 on #1157: "definitely not worth it spending a re-review".** When a
CodeRabbit pass returns only nitpicks and the fix is test-only, comment-only, or otherwise leaves the
production code byte-identical, the head changes but the risk does not. Re-flipping costs a full hour
that the unreviewed PRs behind it need.

Verify the claim from the tree before deciding — `git diff <reviewed-head> <new-head> -- <src-file>`
empty is what makes it a nitpick-only fix, not the agent's say-so.

A slot spent re-confirming a nitpick fix is a slot not spent on a PR with **zero** bot review. That
trade is almost never right while the queue is deep.

## CodeRabbit web runs can freeze — detect it by `updated_at`

On 2026-08-07 #1151's run stamped its status comment at 16:22:31Z reading "Currently processing new
changes…" and then **never touched it again**. A live run edits that comment as it progresses, so a
frozen `updated_at` is the tell — not the "processing" text itself. Forty minutes of the recycle
script's poll window bought nothing and the hour's slot was wasted.

Contrast: #1147 flip→clean verdict in 3 minutes; #1157 flip→findings in 2 minutes. **A healthy web
review is minutes, not tens of minutes.** If `updated_at` has not moved in ~10 minutes, stop waiting.

Recovery: the **CodeRabbit CLI** (`coderabbit review --agent --committed --base-commit <sha>`, v0.7.1,
authenticated) works even while the web run on the same PR is frozen, and **does not consume the web
quota**. It is a stopgap, not a substitute — it under-reports vs a full web review
([[project-coderabbit-cli-underreports-vs-web]]), so a CLI-clean PR is not a reviewed PR. To force a
fresh web run on an unchanged head, flip ready **and** post `@coderabbitai review`; a bare ready-flip
may be ignored when CR already has a run associated with that head.

**The slot is consumed the moment CR stamps the comment, not when it finishes.** On #1157 that was
16 seconds after the flip — too fast to recall by re-drafting. Decide the priority order *before*
flipping; a re-draft never refunds the slot.
