content.text:
**GitHub is down.** Zero of ten REST probes and zero of five GraphQL probes succeeded at 18:35Z.

**The 18:34 slot was not spent.** My script aborted before flipping, so nothing was consumed — the abort message was misleading, not the outcome. It read `HEAD MOVED ( != 2e1696e3c…)` with an empty value, because the head read failed and I had not given it a retry loop. `recycle-both.sh` retries that call five times precisely because a transient empty read is not a moved head; I did not copy that when I wrote the wrapper. Fixed now with eight attempts and an explicit "cannot read" abort that is distinguishable from a real head move.

#1151's head is confirmed still `2e1696e3c`, the commit the CLI already cleared.

I have armed the forced review to fire on GitHub's recovery rather than at a fixed time. It requires **five consecutive successful probes**, not one lucky one, so a flapping recovery does not trigger a flip that then half-fails. If GitHub does not come back within the watch window it reports that and flips nothing.

Nothing to do until GitHub returns. Worth noting for when it does: an API outage does not pause CodeRabbit's hourly clock, so the slot should still be there.

**As of 2026-08-07, CodeRabbit is the only bot reviewer that actually runs on this repo.** Confirmed by
the user, and confirmed empirically: PR #1141 (merged) and #1147 both show reviews from
`coderabbitai[bot]` and the user only — no Greptile review, and macroscope skipped all five agents.

- **Greptile** — quota exhausted; **resets mid-August 2026**. It posts nothing until then. Do not
  wait for a late Greptile sweep on wave-7 PRs and do not report its silence as a clean verdict.
- **macroscope** — out of credits since 2026-08-06. It still registers five check-runs and
  **completes** them all with conclusion `skipped` and the title "Credit balance exhausted".
  `completed` is not `reviewed`; counting completed runs scores a total no-op as full coverage.
  The user has applied to the **macroscope OSS programme** to restore it without paying.
- **CodeRabbit** — working, Pro Plus, CHILL profile, 1 review/hour org-wide.

**The user has decided this batch is CodeRabbit-only.** Do not propose spinning up independent
review sub-agents to compensate — it was offered once and declined. The per-PR `/simplify`,
`/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review` gates already ran during authoring and remain the
floor; see [[feedback-simplify-security-review-mandatory-per-draft-pr]].

Cost is the reason. Keep that in mind before suggesting anything that burns review credits.

## Do not re-review after a nitpick-only fix

**Confirmed by the user 2026-08-07 on #1157: "definitely not worth it spending a re-review".** When a
CodeRabbit pass returns only nitpicks and the fix is test-only, comment-only, or otherwise leaves the
production code byte-identical, the head changes but the risk does not. Re-flipping costs a full hour
that the unreviewed PRs behind it need.

Verify the claim from the tree before deciding — `git diff <reviewed-head> <new-head> -- <src-file>`
empty is what makes it a nitpick-only fix, not the agent's say-so.

A slot spent re-confirming a nitpick fix is a slot not spent on a PR with **zero** bot review. That
trade is almost never right while the queue is deep.

## CodeRabbit web runs can freeze — detect it by `updated_at`

On 2026-08-07 #1151's run stamped its status comment at 16:22:31Z reading "Currently processing new
changes…" and then **never touched it again**. A live run edits that comment as it progresses, so a
frozen `updated_at` is the tell — not the "processing" text itself. Forty minutes of the recycle
script's poll window bought nothing and the hour's slot was wasted.

Contrast: #1147 flip→clean verdict in 3 minutes; #1157 flip→findings in 2 minutes. **A healthy web
review is minutes, not tens of minutes.** If `updated_at` has not moved in ~10 minutes, stop waiting.

Recovery: the **CodeRabbit CLI** (`coderabbit review --agent --committed --base-commit <sha>`, v0.7.1,
authenticated) works even while the web run on the same PR is frozen, and **does not consume the web
quota**. It is a stopgap, not a substitute — it under-reports vs a full web review
([[project-coderabbit-cli-underreports-vs-web]]), so a CLI-clean PR is not a reviewed PR. To force a
fresh web run on an unchanged head, flip ready **and** post `@coderabbitai review`; a bare ready-flip
may be ignored when CR already has a run associated with that head.

**The slot is consumed the moment CR stamps the comment, not when it finishes.** On #1157 that was
16 seconds after the flip — too fast to recall by re-drafting. Decide the priority order *before*
flipping; a re-draft never refunds the slot.

Related: [[project-macroscope-third-pr-reviewer]], [[project-greptile-second-pr-reviewer]],
[[feedback-coderabbit-web-review-auto-and-rate-limited]].

**#1151's full web review: 1 actionable comment, and it is a fair one.**

The doc on `CommandOutcome` read "What a command handed back across the worker boundary" — an incomplete sentence that describes what the type does rather than telling a host anything useful.

I did not take CodeRabbit's proposed replacement ("Hosts need a discriminated result to handle each command outcome"), because that is just a different "what" sentence and does not match how this file documents anything else. Instead I matched the file's own convention: `Event` has the identical `kind`-plus-payload-getter shape and reads "One event the engine emits… Read `kind`, then the matching payload getter." So `CommandOutcome` now reads:

> The result of one `Engine::command` call. Read `kind`, then the matching payload getter.

That tells a host the actual access pattern, which is the thing worth knowing.

Gates are running on the change.

**One thing I noticed but did not fix, because it is outside the finding.** `CommandOutcome` is placed directly under the `// Snapshot read surface — key-free view state projected by the engine` banner, but a command result is not snapshot read surface. The PR introduced the type there. Moving it above that banner would be a two-line change and would stop the section header from being wrong. Say the word and I will fold it into the same commit; otherwise I leave it, since expanding scope on a review fix is how the unrelated-churn problems start.

The bigger takeaway from this round: the CLI said 0 findings on this exact commit and the full web review found 1. Same head, same files. That is the under-reporting gap measured directly, and it is why I would not let the CLI stand in for a web verdict on #1156 or #1158.

---
name: feedback-never-write-a-closing-keyword-to-negate-it
description: "Writing 'Does not close #NNNN' in a PR body still auto-closes the issue — GitHub's parser ignores the negation"

**Never put a closing keyword next to an issue number in a PR body to say the opposite.**

On 2026-08-07 I edited PR #1151 to stop it closing #1016, replacing `Closes #1016` with the sentence
"Does **not** close #1016." GitHub's linked-issue parser matches `close|closes|closed|fix|fixes|
fixed|resolve|resolves|resolved` followed by `#N` **anywhere in the body and ignores the negation**,
so the merge closed #1016 anyway — while five open blockers remained on it. The exact phrasing meant
to prevent the close is what caused it.

**How to apply:** to reference an issue a PR does *not* close, rephrase so no keyword touches the
number — "the remaining arms are tracked in #1016", "see #1016" — or escape the reference. Then
**verify after the merge** that the issue is still open; the failure is silent and only shows up as a
wrongly-closed tracker item, which in turn falsely unblocks everything downstream of it (#1167 lost
its blocker until #1016 was reopened).

Same family as [[feedback-closes-vs-part-of-issue-hygiene]]: the tracker graph is only as honest as
the keywords in the PR body, and a wrong one fails toward "done".

content.text:
All five findings are in hand, and one is substantive.

**The major one is real and worth the PR.** After `commit_write()` succeeds, the code pushes only `Invalidation::Attributes`. That tells the kernel the metadata changed, but not that the *bytes* did — so another open handle on the same inode can keep serving cached pages from the pre-commit version. On a filesystem whose whole job is to publish what the user wrote, serving stale bytes after a successful commit is a correctness defect, not a nit.

Two more are honest narrowing of claims the code no longer earns, and both point at the same limitation I filed as #1162: the doc says a whole-block writer pays no resolve, and the "never blocks" test only proves that for a *created* handle, because `create` pre-inserts `Pending::over(0)`. A handle reopened on a file with an unprojected size does call `base_len`, which awaits `render` and `stream_for`.

**As of 2026-08-07, CodeRabbit is the only bot reviewer that actually runs on this repo.** Confirmed by
the user, and confirmed empirically: PR #1141 (merged) and #1147 both show reviews from
`coderabbitai[bot]` and the user only — no Greptile review, and macroscope skipped all five agents.

- **Greptile** — quota exhausted; **resets mid-August 2026**. It posts nothing until then. Do not
  wait for a late Greptile sweep on wave-7 PRs and do not report its silence as a clean verdict.
- **macroscope** — out of credits since 2026-08-06. It still registers five check-runs and
  **completes** them all with conclusion `skipped` and the title "Credit balance exhausted".
  `completed` is not `reviewed`; counting completed runs scores a total no-op as full coverage.
  The user has applied to the **macroscope OSS programme** to restore it without paying.
- **CodeRabbit** — working, Pro Plus, CHILL profile, 1 review/hour org-wide.

**The user has decided this batch is CodeRabbit-only.** Do not propose spinning up independent
review sub-agents to compensate — it was offered once and declined. The per-PR `/simplify`,
`/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review` gates already ran during authoring and remain the
floor; see [[feedback-simplify-security-review-mandatory-per-draft-pr]].

Cost is the reason. Keep that in mind before suggesting anything that burns review credits.

## Do not re-review after a nitpick-only fix

**Confirmed by the user 2026-08-07 on #1157: "definitely not worth it spending a re-review".** When a
CodeRabbit pass returns only nitpicks and the fix is test-only, comment-only, or otherwise leaves the
production code byte-identical, the head changes but the risk does not. Re-flipping costs a full hour
that the unreviewed PRs behind it need.

Verify the claim from the tree before deciding — `git diff <reviewed-head> <new-head> -- <src-file>`
empty is what makes it a nitpick-only fix, not the agent's say-so.

A slot spent re-confirming a nitpick fix is a slot not spent on a PR with **zero** bot review. That
trade is almost never right while the queue is deep.

## CodeRabbit web runs can freeze — detect it by `updated_at`

On 2026-08-07 #1151's run stamped its status comment at 16:22:31Z reading "Currently processing new
changes…" and then **never touched it again**. A live run edits that comment as it progresses, so a
frozen `updated_at` is the tell — not the "processing" text itself. Forty minutes of the recycle
script's poll window bought nothing and the hour's slot was wasted.

Contrast: #1147 flip→clean verdict in 3 minutes; #1157 flip→findings in 2 minutes. **A healthy web
review is minutes, not tens of minutes.** If `updated_at` has not moved in ~10 minutes, stop waiting.

Recovery: the **CodeRabbit CLI** (`coderabbit review --agent --committed --base-commit <sha>`, v0.7.1,
authenticated) works even while the web run on the same PR is frozen, and **does not consume the web
quota**. It is a stopgap, not a substitute — it under-reports vs a full web review
([[project-coderabbit-cli-underreports-vs-web]]), so a CLI-clean PR is not a reviewed PR.

**On an unchanged head, `@coderabbitai review` does NOTHING — use `@coderabbitai full review`.**
Learned the hard way on #1151 (2026-08-07): after its first run froze, a ready-flip plus
`@coderabbitai review` produced only a 390-byte reply saying there were no new commits to review,
because plain `review` covers commits *since the last review*. `full review` re-reviews the whole
diff from scratch and is the only thing that works when the head has not moved. A bare ready-flip is
likewise ignored when CR already has a run associated with that head.

**The slot is consumed the moment CR stamps the comment, not when it finishes.** On #1157 that was
16 seconds after the flip — too fast to recall by re-drafting. Decide the priority order *before*
flipping; a re-draft never refunds the slot.

Related: [[project-macroscope-third-pr-reviewer]], [[project-greptile-second-pr-reviewer]],
[[feedback-coderabbit-web-review-auto-and-rate-limited]].

content.text:
That fits, and it confirms the correction rather than complicating it. Marking #1156 ready in order to merge it triggered a CodeRabbit review attempt at ~21:22Z, which was refused — and the refusal reported 26 minutes remaining, putting the reset at ~21:48Z. That is exactly 60 minutes after #1156's review **started** at 20:48:34, not 60 minutes after its verdict at 20:55:52. So the window is start-based, as the reschedule assumes.

Two practical consequences:

The refusal cost nothing — a rejected attempt does not consume a slot, so 21:50 is genuinely clear for #1149.

And flipping a draft to ready purely to merge it will provoke a review attempt every time. Harmless when the limit refuses it, but if a slot happens to be free at that moment it would spend it on a PR you are about to merge. For #1158, #1145 and #1146, the safe order is to let the cycle review and re-draft first, then flip and merge — which is what we have been doing.

#1149 is armed for 21:50:30Z.

content.content:
=== #1159 title + scope ===
engine: an assumed first-run placement must not latch the account BYO flag
---
Found by the `/crypto-privacy-review` gate on the #1084 PR. The fix belongs in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, which #1084's batch did not own, so it is filed rather than folded in.

## The defect

`hosted_quota_pre_flight` reconciles the account's BYO flag once per session:

```rust
if !self.byo_reconciled.get()
    && quota.advisory == hosted_leg
    && api.set_byo(!hosted_leg).await.is_ok()
```

It returns early on `Err(refusal)`, so only a placement that *resolved* reaches this line. After #1084 the only degraded placement that resolves is `DefaultsReason::UnprovenFirstRun` — the assumed first-run default, which is `Placement::Hosted`, so `hosted_leg = true`.

Chain:

1. Device A picks `External` and publishes. Its first write reconciles `advisory=false == hosted_leg=false` and PATCHes `byo=true`. The account flag is now true.
2. Device B is a fresh install on the same account. An adversary who controls the record-plane leg withholds the settings record. B holds none of the durable marks #1084 added, so the load reports `UnprovenFirstRun` and the placement is the assumed `Hosted`.
3. B's first write sees `advisory=true == hosted_leg=true` and PATCHes `byo=false`.


=== is there an issue for the withholding/positive-evidence gap? ===
1084 OPEN engine: stop a withheld settings record placing a fresh device on the hosted default
1159 OPEN engine: an assumed first-run placement must not latch the account BYO flag

Both changes are in and the gates are running.

**#1149's review: 1 Minor finding, and it was worth having.** The test called `expect_err` with no type check, so a refusal *earlier* than the head-block upload would have satisfied it — the mint counter would already be raised, the later `Suppressed` assertion would still hold, and the test would pass without ever exercising the thing it claims to. The status, the attack chain, and the "closing that needs…" roadmap now live solely in #1159, which already held them.

That is also a small win against a recurring problem in this repo: the spec was carrying prose that would have become false the moment #1159 landed, with nothing in CI to catch the drift.

Once the gates pass I will push, reply to and resolve the thread, and wait for CI. Then **#1158** — the largest PR of the wave, and the one that owns the `write_plane.rs` append-both resolve, which gets cheaper if #1149 merges first.

They are the workflow's own readiness loop — `curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1` at `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml:122` — printing while it waits. ## Why it matters

The gate is required, so a flake is not cosmetic: it stops a merge. During wave 7 it cost a re-run cycle on #1158 and the diagnosis time to prove the Rust diff was not responsible. As more slices land on this harness the cost compounds, and a required check that fails randomly trains reviewers to re-run without reading — which is exactly how a real regression gets waved through.

## Scope

- Find why the first navigation to `/` can leave the login controls not visible within 5s while a sibling navigation in the same run is fine. Likely candidates: the preview server's first response after the bundle build, app hydration, or a cold worker on the first page load.
- Fix the root cause rather than raising the timeout. A longer timeout hides the first-load cost instead of removing it, and this suite is a merge gate.
- If a wait is genuinely required, make it an explicit readiness condition the harness asserts once, not a per-assertion timeout.
- Cover both signatures; a fix for A that leaves B is not done.

## Acceptance

- The smoke slice passes on 20 consecutive runs with no re-run.
- No assertion timeout was raised to achieve it.
- The failure mode, if it recurs, names the unmet readiness condition rather than a bare `toBeVisible` timeout.

## Gate

`Web E2E Smoke Result`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user drove a multi-stage wave-7 execution session on the CipherBox v2 rewrite:

1. **"please kick off wave 7 batches"** — launch the planned wave-7 work as parallel background agents.
2. **"why are there 11 prs when there were only meant to be 6? this is going to be a major pain to review at 1 pr per hour."** — challenge the PR count against review throughput.
3. **"yeah please consolidate what can be consolidated and advise the new merge order."**
4. **"ok now you can start handling the reviews using the bash script in the repo scratchpad in merge order. there should already be a coderabbit slot available right now to start with"**
5. Confirm whether I will handle adding the wasm job to required contexts post-merge; informed me this batch is **CodeRabbit-only** (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug; macroscope OSS application pending) because of cost.
6. **"no re-review needed"** on nitpick-only fixes; rebase each PR before its review.
7. **"is the residual from #1149 being tracked anywhere? ... this is honestly the wrong place to do so in my books. This repo tracks residuals in github issues that are edged and parented."** → **"yes, cut the residual passage after the review lands"**
8. **"isnt there already an issue to investigate and resolve the flake in the web-e2e test?"**

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **File-ownership batching** — the binding constraint on PR parallelism is hot-file contention, not issue count. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` was contended by 7 day-one issues.
- **Semantic merge conflicts** — two branches both `MERGEABLE` that break `main` when merged pairwise; `git merge-tree` for textual scan, cumulative merge + `cargo check` for semantic.
- **CodeRabbit web review economics** — 1 review/hour org-wide; the hour runs from when a review **starts**, not when its verdict lands; slot consumed the moment CR stamps its comment.
- **`@coderabbitai review` vs `@coderabbitai full review`** — plain `review` covers only commits *since the last review*, so it is a no-op on an unchanged head.
- **Frozen CodeRabbit runs** — detected by an unchanged `updated_at` on the status comment, not by the "Currently processing" text.
- **CodeRabbit CLI** (`coderabbit review --agent --committed --base-commit <sha>`, v0.7.1) — does not consume the web quota, but under-reports (proved: 0 findings vs web's 1 on the same commit).
- **GitHub branch protection** — `strict=false` (no forced up-to-date); skipped required checks satisfy protection (proved by #1113 merging with `Web Bundle: SKIPPED`).
- **GitHub linked-issue keyword parsing** — matches `close #NNNN` even inside a negation.
- **Rust workspace gates** — `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- **TS gates** — `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`.
- **AGENTS.md rule 8** — encode/decode fail-closed symmetry; release-active `Err`, never `debug_assert!`.
- **Comment law** — comments explain *why*; no absence-justifying comments, no unchanged-code apologia, no tracker references.
- **GitHub sub-issues/dependencies APIs** — keyed by **database id**, not number; REST `.parent` is always null (use `parent_issue_url`).

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/wave7-brief.md` (created)
Shared brief read by all 8 batch agents. Contains: the file-ownership table (B1–B8), worktree/build hygiene (no shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `pnpm install` not symlink), the zsh-no-`PIPESTATUS` warning, gate commands, code law, review-gate requirements, git/PR rules. Later amended with:
- Review sub-agent rules: **no git write commands** (a reviewer ran `git checkout --` and destroyed 3 in-flight edits); **never report a verdict before its validation returned**.
- Follow-up issue hygiene (labels + component label + milestone + parent + edge).
- "Before you call a merge safe" — `git merge-tree` between sibling branches.

### `/Users/myankelev/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/recycle-both.sh`
The user's review-cycle script. Takes `$1 = PR`, `$2 = earliest epoch to flip`. Sequence: retry-read head (5 attempts) → wait for CI (`MINCHECKS` floor, excludes CodeRabbit/Macroscope from pending) → wait for `NOTBEFORE` → flip ready (confirmed) → poll 40× 60s for CR verdict (both review-body and clean-status-comment surfaces) and macroscope → re-draft (confirmed) → print RESULT.

I edited it (raising `MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}` to `30`) **while an instance was running**, which corrupted the running process at line 119. File on disk verified fine with `bash -n`.

### `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/cycle-when-healthy.sh` (created)
Wrapper requiring **8 consecutive** successful GitHub API probes before `exec bash recycle-both.sh "$PR" "$NOTBEFORE"`. Written after GitHub outages/flapping aborted two runs.

### `/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/force-1151.sh` (created, then patched)
Forces a fresh review on an unchanged head: wait for slot → verify head unchanged → flip → post `@coderabbitai review` → poll → re-draft. **Original bug:** no retry on the head read, so a transient empty read printed `HEAD MOVED ( != 2e1696e3c...)` and aborted. Patched to 8 retries with a distinct "CANNOT READ HEAD" abort.

### `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs` (#1151 fix)
```rust
/// The result of one `Engine::command` call. Read `kind`, then the matching
/// payload getter.
#[wasm_bindgen]
pub struct CommandOutcome {
```
Replaced `/// What a command handed back across the worker boundary.` Matched the file's `Event` convention rather than CodeRabbit's proposed "Hosts need a discriminated result…".

### `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` (#1149 fix)
```rust
    let refused_save = block_on(publish_settings(
        ...
    ))
    .expect_err("the save does not reach the network");
    // Scoped to a publish failure: an earlier refusal would leave the mint
    // counter raised without ever attempting the head block this test counts.
    assert!(
        matches!(refused_save, SettingsPublishError::Publish(_)),
        "the head-block publish must be what failed, got {refused_save:?}"
    );
```
Import widened to:
```rust
use cipherbox_engine::settings::{
    Destinations, SettingsPublishError, VaultSettings, publish_settings, settings_name,
};
```

### `blueprint/engine.md` (#1149 trim)
Cut a 13-line `Residual:` passage down to 5 lines of normative rule:
```
  lost one. Absence is a verdict about _this device_ only, so an assumed
  placement must never latch account-scoped state, and the account's advisory
  BYO flag may only ever be read in the restricting direction — `advisory` set
  means never assume the default. The inverse would be a server-controlled
  widening on an untrusted signal.
```

### `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` (#1156 fix, by agent)
Added `self.adapter.invalidate(Invalidation::Data { ino });` before `Invalidation::Attributes` in `commit`. Test `published::a_commit_repaints_the_pages_of_the_version_it_replaced` fails without it.

### `scripts/check-tracker-refs.mjs` (read)
`const ROOTS = ['crates', 'apps', 'packages', 'landing', 'tools', 'scripts', '.github'];` and `EXTENSIONS = /\.(rs|ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|toml|json|ya?ml|sh)$/` — so `blueprint/*.md` is **not** scanned.

### Memory files created/updated
- `project-wave7-planning-state.md` — rewritten with the 8-batch ownership table, consolidation record, merge order, and the facade-contention finding.
- `project-pr-reviewer-availability-aug-2026.md` (new) — CodeRabbit-only; no re-review after nitpick-only fixes; frozen-run detection; start-based hour; `full review` vs `review`.
- `feedback-review-subagents-no-git-writes.md` (new)
- `feedback-never-write-a-closing-keyword-to-negate-it.md` (new)
- `project-windows-linker-1104-flake.md` (new)
- `project-web-e2e-smoke-signout-test-flaky.md` — **was mid-edit when summary requested**; edit succeeded, adding the #1169 tracking pointer, both signatures, the dispositive `smoke.spec.ts:14` check, and the "curl retry loop is not the cause" note.

## 4. Errors and Fixes

`Web E2E Smoke Result` became a **required** status check on `main` on 2026-08-05. It flakes.

First observed 2026-08-06 on PR #1103 — an **engine-only Rust PR touching no web code**.
`tests/web-e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts:43`, *"signing out returns the tab to the front door"*, timed
out after 1.5 minutes on `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/$/)`. The other four tests in the suite
passed. **Re-running the same commit with no change turned it green**, which is what makes it a
flake rather than a defect in the PR.

Corroboration that it was not the PR: on the same night all six sibling PRs passed the gate,
including the two that actually change `apps/web`.

**Why it matters:** a flaky *required* check intermittently blocks merges on PRs with no
relationship to the web. It is also the newest required context, so it has the least track record.
Historical `web-e2e.yml` runs show repeated failure clusters on the same branch, so flakiness in
this suite predates the smoke slice.

**How to apply:** when a wave-5-or-later PR fails only `Web E2E Smoke`, check whether siblings pass
before investigating the diff. Re-run before triaging — `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. Note the
called workflow cannot be re-run standalone (`workflow_call` from `ci.yml`); target the parent CI
run id, and expect a misleading "its workflow file may be broken" message even when the rerun does
in fact start.

**TRACKED as #1169 since 2026-08-08** — parented under #995, `comp:ci`, milestone v2.0.0. It had
lived only in this note until then, which was the defect: a known break with no edged, parented
issue. Add new observations to #1169 rather than re-diagnosing from scratch.

**Two signatures, not one.** (A) `smoke.spec.ts:6` "the front door offers every built login method"
fails on `expect(login.googleButton).toBeVisible()` — seen 2026-08-07 on #1158, a Rust-only prune PR.
(B) the sign-out test above. Either can fire alone; B passed in the run where A failed.

**The dispositive check, cheaper than reading any log:** `smoke.spec.ts:14` asserts the *same*
`googleButton` locator as `:6` and passed in the same run that `:6` failed. One locator, two tests,
opposite outcomes — that is timing, and it rules out a real regression outright.

**Not the cause:** `curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 3000/3001` in the log is the
workflow's own readiness loop — `curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1` at
`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml:122` — printing while it waits. The API is up before Playwright runs.
Do not chase it as a broken stack.

Fixing the flake belongs with the write-path e2e work (the suite currently starts no Kubo, which is
the standing gap in that slice). Related:
[[project-web-e2e-only-on-main-push]], [[project-desktop-build-matrix-context-deadlock]],
[[project-windows-linker-1104-flake]].

description: "Cargo Check & Test (Windows) can fail with link.exe exit 1104 on cipherbox-core's kat_gen example — transient, re-run it"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  modified: 2026-08-07T22:08:41.263Z
---

`Cargo Check & Test (Windows)` — a **required** context — can fail with:

```
error: linking with `link.exe` failed: exit code: 1104
error: could not compile `cipherbox-core` (example "kat_gen") due to 1 previous error
```

Seen 2026-08-07 on PR #1149 at head `4b8d1246a`. Exit 1104 from `link.exe` is a runner
resource/file-access failure, not a code defect. A plain re-run of the failed job went green with no
change to the diff.

**How to tell it apart from a real break, before touching the diff:** check whether the same job
passed on the PR's *previous* head. On #1149 the two new commits were a test assertion and a markdown
trim — neither can affect linking a `cipherbox-core` example — and `52dce2085` had Windows green.
That comparison is the cheap disambiguation; do it first.

**Gotcha:** `gh run rerun <id> --failed` is refused while the overall run is still `in_progress`
("cannot be rerun; its workflow file may be broken" — a misleading message). One Windows job can be
`completed/failure` while sibling jobs still run. Wait for the run to reach `completed`, then re-run.

Second known flaky required check alongside
[[project-web-e2e-smoke-signout-test-flaky]]. Re-run before triaging either.

skills.content:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash
gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO_NAME/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable

# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.

GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)

Overnight plan is armed. Three things are running:

**#1158** — cycle `bzc2vrmsb`, CI green at `319341e36` (26 checks settled), flips ready at **22:49:07Z** for its CodeRabbit slot.

**#1145 → #1146** — chained in `bv4m9egnk`. Each PR's slot is derived from the *previous flip*, not the previous verdict, because the hour runs from when a review starts. So #1145 flips ~23:53Z and #1146 ~00:54Z. The chain retries on a rate-limit comment rather than losing the PR: a flip inside the cooldown gets answered with "Review limit reached" instead of a review, and consumes no slot, so a retry is free where a silent skip would cost the PR its verdict entirely.

All three are rebased onto current `main` (`8c69c17c7`) and `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`.

**The check worth flagging:** you plan to merge all three in the morning, but each is only rebased against `main` *individually*. Their file lists are fully disjoint — #1158 is Rust-only under `crates/`, #1145 is `packages/client/src/worker/`, #1146 is `apps/web/` plus `packages/client/src/media/`. That rules out a textual conflict but not a semantic one, and there is a specific reason to suspect one here: **#1145 makes an unknown worker command fail closed, and #1146 adds a media broker that issues worker commands.** If #1146 introduces a command kind that #1145's new rejection path does not know, both PRs stay green alone and `main` breaks on the second merge.

I merged all three cumulatively — clean, at `fe9251680` — and the full gate set is running against that tree now (`bvcgqndr1`): both toolchains, since a cross-language break would only show in one.

I will fold in each verdict as it lands. Per your standing call I will not request a re-review for nitpick-only fixes, and I will leave each PR re-drafted so nothing collects an unplanned review overnight — they will need a ready-flip before you merge.

#!/bin/bash
# Overnight chain: drive #1145 then #1146 through recycle-both.sh, one CodeRabbit
# slot each. The hourly slot runs from when a review STARTS, so each PR's earliest
# flip is derived from the PREVIOUS flip, not from the previous verdict.
#   $1 = epoch of the flip that consumed the current slot (i.e. #1158's flip)
set -u
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"
RECYCLE=/Users/myankelev/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/recycle-both.sh
LOGDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/2b9a962d-e9c8-4465-b4ef-93584f21a390/scratchpad
PREV_FLIP=$1

# recycle-both.sh prints the flip as a bare HH:MM:SSZ, so the date has to be put
# back on it. A reconstruction that lands in the future belongs to yesterday.
flip_epoch_from_log() {
  local t
  t=$(grep -m1 -oE "FLIPPED READY [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z" "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}')
  if [ -z "$t" ]; then date -u +%s; return; fi
  local now e
  now=$(date -u +%s)
  e=$(date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)T${t}" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")
  [ "$e" -gt "$now" ] && e=$((e - 86400))
  echo "$e"
}

for PR in 1145 1146; do
  NB=$((PREV_FLIP + 3660))
  LOG=""
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    LOG="$LOGDIR/cycle-$PR-$attempt.log"
    echo "=== #$PR attempt $attempt, notbefore=$(date -u -r "$NB" +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
    MINCHECKS=25 bash "$RECYCLE" "$PR" "$NB" >"$LOG" 2>&1
    echo "#$PR cycle rc=$? (log $LOG)"
    tail -6 "$LOG"

    # A flip inside the cooldown is answered with a rate-limit comment instead of a
    # review. No slot is consumed, so retry rather than lose the PR to a silent skip.
    LIMU=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments \
      --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
    LIMEP=0
    [ -n "$LIMU" ] && LIMEP=$(date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "$LIMU" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "$LIMEP" -gt "$NB" ] 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "#$PR RATE LIMITED (cr limit comment at $LIMU) - retrying in 21m"
      NB=$(( $(date -u +%s) + 1260 ))
      continue
    fi
    break
  done
  PREV_FLIP=$(flip_epoch_from_log "$LOG")
  echo "#$PR flip epoch=$PREV_FLIP ($(date -u -r "$PREV_FLIP" +%H:%M:%SZ))"
done

echo "=== CHAIN COMPLETE $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
for PR in 1145 1146; do
  echo "#$PR isDraft=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft')"
done

**A failed `owe_retires` loses the reclaim debt permanently.**

`publish_node` at Line 1711 passes `Some(applied.op_id)` as `completes`, so the published-op mark is raised the moment the record acks. If `owe_retires` at Line 1726 then fails with a seam error, `publish_prune` returns `Err(Halt::Unclassified)` and the op stays queued, but the shortened history is already live. Two outcomes follow:

- The pass retries the op. `plan_prune` now sees the shortened history, `plan.retire_targets` is empty, and Line 1674 returns `Ok(())`. The dropped roots are never journaled.
- The device restarts. The published-op mark drops the op as already published, with the same result.

The dropped versions then stay pinned and charged to the account forever, and `pending_reclaim_bytes` never reports them. This is a leak rather than data loss, which matches the crate's stated preference, but the ledger is the only record of the debt and this path silently discards it.

Consider journaling the owed entries before the publish and treating a pre-publish ledger entry as advisory, or retrying `owe_retires` within the pass before returning.

Found by the CodeRabbit gate on #1158 and confirmed against the branch at `319341e36`. Filed rather than fixed in that PR: the obvious fix trades a bounded leak for possible data loss, which inverts the crate's stated preference, and the safe fix is a seam change.

## The mechanism

`Drain::publish_prune` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`) publishes the shortened record, then journals what that dropped:

1. `publish_node(.., Some(applied.op_id))` — `publish_node` calls `mark_published(scope, op_id)` the moment `publish_head` acks. Its own doc states the ack, not the adopt, is where the op stops being replayable.
2. `owe_retires(scope, &plan.retire_targets)` — journals the dropped roots to the `RetireLedger`.

If step 2 fails with a seam error, `publish_prune` returns `Err`, but the shortened history is already live and the op is already marked published. Both continuations lose the debt:

- **Retry in the same pass.** `plan_prune` re-reads the now-shortened history, `plan.retire_targets` is empty, and the early return fires. Nothing is journaled.
- **Restart.** The published-op mark drops the op as already published, with the same result.

The dropped versions stay pinned and charged to the account with nothing naming them, and `pending_reclaim_bytes` never reports them. The ledger is the only record of the debt, and this path discards it silently.

## Why a replay cannot recover it

`crates/engine/src/seams/retire_ledger.rs` states the invariant that makes this terminal:

> once the shortened history publishes, nothing readable names the dropped roots, while a root always names its own leaves

So no later pass can reconstruct the doomed set from the record. Any failure after the publish is unrecoverable for that debt, not merely delayed.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong

The reviewer proposed journaling the owed entries before the publish. That is unsafe as the ledger stands. `drain_owed_retires` (`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs`) retires every entry it reads with no check that the CID is unreachable, so an entry written before the publish can be acted on while a resolvable record still names the root. That unpins live content.

The crate ranks these outcomes explicitly, in `orphaned_head` in the same file:

> No ack is not proof nothing stored: unpinning a head a live record may still name is loss, where the row is only a leak.

The current ordering is therefore correct as written, and the doc comment on `publish_prune` states that rationale. The hole is the failure window it opens, not the order itself.

Retrying `owe_retires` in-pass — the reviewer's other suggestion — narrows the window but does not close it. A crash between the two steps, or a staging store that stays down, still loses the debt.

## What a real fix needs

An owed entry must be safe to hold while the old record is still live, so it can be journaled first. That means an unconfirmed state the drain skips, confirmed after the publish acks — a change to `OwedRetire`, to the `RetireLedger` trait, and to the conformance kit in `testkit::conformance::retire_ledger` that pins its contract.

An alternative worth weighing first: have `drain_owed_retires` establish unreachability itself before retiring, which would make a pre-publish entry harmless without a schema change, at the cost of a resolve per entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `RetireLedger::owe` failure after the record acks leaves the debt recoverable, and a later pass retires the dropped roots.
- The same holds across a process restart between the publish and the journal.
- No path retires a root that a resolvable record still names.
- `pending_reclaim_bytes` reports the debt for the whole window it is owed.
- A test drives the failure injection rather than asserting on source text.

## Scope note

The leak is bounded by what one prune drops and needs the staging store to fail in a narrow window, so this does not block the prune slice from landing.

**The actionable finding is real, and I did not apply its suggested fix — that fix would make things worse.** The mechanism checks out: `publish_node` calls `mark_published` the moment the record acks, so the op stops being replayable *before* `owe_retires` journals the debt. If the journal fails, the shortened history is already live. `retire_ledger.rs` states why that is terminal rather than merely delayed — once the shortened history publishes, nothing readable names the dropped roots, so no retry can reconstruct the doomed set. The dropped versions stay pinned and charged with nothing pointing at them.

Its fallback suggestion (retry in-pass) narrows the window without closing it — a crash still loses the debt.

A correct fix needs an owed entry that is safe to hold while the old record is live: an unconfirmed state the drain skips. That changes `OwedRetire`, the `RetireLedger` trait, and the conformance kit pinning its contract — its own change, not something to push unreviewed overnight.

---

🌐 Web query:

`MDN HTMLMediaElement crossOrigin src download fetch start src load browser behavior`

💡 Result:

The crossOrigin attribute on an HTMLMediaElement (such as video or audio) functions as a CORS settings attribute, controlling how the browser handles cross-origin requests for the media resource [1][2][3]. When set, it determines the CORS mode and credentials mode used during the resource fetch process [1][4]. If the attribute is omitted, the browser performs a non-CORS request, which may result in the resource being marked as tainted if accessed cross-origin [2][3]. The behavior is summarized as follows: 1. Anonymous: When set to anonymous (or an empty string), the browser uses the CORS mode for the fetch [1][4]. If the resource is from the same origin, it behaves like a standard request; if it is cross-origin, it initiates a CORS request without sending user credentials (like cookies or HTTP authentication) [1][2][3]. 2. Use-Credentials: When set to use-credentials, the browser uses the CORS mode and includes user credentials (cookies, client certificates) in the request [1][4]. This is necessary if the media server requires authentication to access the file, regardless of whether the domain is the same or cross-origin [2][3]. The crossOrigin attribute must be placed directly on the media element (e.g., <video crossorigin="anonymous" src="...">), not on the individual <source> elements, as it reflects the properties of the HTMLMediaElement itself [5][6][7]. If a resource is fetched without appropriate CORS headers and the crossOrigin attribute is not properly configured, the media may be considered tainted. This prevents the media data from being read or manipulated by scripts (e.g., drawing video frames to a <canvas> element) [2][8][3]. The fetch process for the src is triggered when the src attribute is set or changed, or when the load method is invoked, and the browser respects the current crossOrigin setting at that time [5][9].

Citations:

- 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/crossOrigin
- 2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/crossorigin
- 3: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/video
- 4: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/htmlmediaelement/crossorigin/index.md
- 5: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html
- 6: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31176124/using-video-with-source-where-do-you-add-the-crossorigin-attribute
- 7: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/dev/media.html
- 8: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html
- 9: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement

---

🌐 Web query:

`MDN HTMLMediaElement error event load src fetch started resource fetched failed src attribute`

💡 Result:

The error event on an HTMLMediaElement is triggered when a media resource fails to load or playback, such as due to network issues, decoding errors, or unsupported source formats [1][2]. When this event occurs, the media element's error property provides a MediaError object containing details about the failure [3][4]. This object includes a code property, which indicates the general nature of the error [5][6]: 1. MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED (1): The user agent aborted the resource fetching process, typically due to a user request [5][7]. 2. MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK (2): A network error prevented the resource from being fetched after it was initially established as usable [5][7]. 3. MEDIA_ERR_DECODE (3): An error occurred during the decoding of the media resource, despite the browser previously determining it was usable [5][7]. 4. MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED (4): The resource specified by the src attribute or a media provider object was found to be unsuitable (e.g., unsupported codec or format) [5][7]. To troubleshoot media loading issues: - Check the MediaError.message property for browser-specific diagnostic information [3][6]. - Use the load method if you dynamically update the src attribute or child source elements; calling load resets the media element and forces it to re-select and re-load the resource [8]. - For deeper debugging, browser-specific tools like the Chrome DevTools "Media" panel can provide detailed logs, events, and warnings that may not be exposed through the standard API [6].

Citations:

- 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/error_event
- 2: https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/htmlmediaelement/error_event/index.md
- 3: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaError
- 4: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/error

</details>

**Subscribe before mounting the media element.**

`MediaPlayer` renders `<audio>`/`<video>` with `src` before the passive `useEffect` subscribes to `MediaService.onStreamError`; the browser can start fetching the URL before that listener exists. If a recoverable stream-ceiling failure is emitted in that window, `onError` can later overwrite it with terminal `FAULT_NOTICE`, and the retry control disappears. Register the failure listener before mounting the media element, and keep a URL-scoped readiness state so `onError` only affects the current mount. Add a runtime test that reports a recoverable refusal during initial mount and asserts that the retry control appears.

Resolve the 3 CodeRabbit review findings on PR #1146 of the CipherBox repo (FSM1/cipher-box). Work ONLY in this worktree:

## The 3 findings (all unresolved threads)

**A. `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/MediaPlayer.tsx:48` — 🟠 Major, functional correctness.**
threadId `PRRT_kwDOQ6DXvM6XbPNz`, comment dbid `3739588751`.
Claim: MediaPlayer renders `<audio>`/`<video>` with `src` BEFORE the passive `useEffect` subscribes to `MediaService.onStreamError`, so the browser can start fetching before the listener exists. If a recoverable stream-ceiling refusal is emitted in that window, the element's `onError` can later overwrite it with a terminal `FAULT_NOTICE` and the retry control disappears.
Reviewer's proposed fix: register the failure listener before mounting the media element, keep a URL-scoped readiness state so `onError` only affects the current mount, and add a runtime test for a recoverable refusal during initial mount asserting the retry control appears.

**VERIFY THIS BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING.** Read MediaPlayer.tsx, the MediaService `onStreamError` implementation, and the broker. Answer concretely:
- Can `onStreamError` actually fire before the effect runs? Does the service buffer/replay the last failure to a late subscriber, or is the event lost?
- Does `onError` genuinely overwrite a recoverable refusal with a terminal one, or is there already precedence logic guarding it?
If the race cannot occur, say so with file:line evidence and push back on the thread instead of inventing a fix. A false positive that gets "fixed" is worse than one that gets refuted. If it IS real, fix it minimally — do not restructure the component.

**B. `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/FileBrowserActions.test.tsx:835` — 🟡 Minor.**
threadId `PRRT_kwDOQ6DXvM6XbPNw`, comment dbid `3739588746`.
The test claims saves are sequential, but `whenStreamIdle` resolves immediately in that harness, so a parallel implementation mints the same two tickets and revokes both and the assertions still pass. Gate the idle result on the test and assert only one ticket is live while the batch runs. `fakePipe` in `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileDownload.test.ts` already uses that shape — follow it.

**C. `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileDownload.test.ts:224` — 🟡 Minor.**
threadId `PRRT_kwDOQ6DXvM6XbPN8`, comment dbid `3739588758`.
Two mismatches: the hook schedules revocation at `REVOKE_AFTER_MS = 1_000` but the test advances 60 s, so a regression changing the delay to 59 s would still pass; and the test name says "rather than at unmount" but never unmounts. Fix by advancing to the real delay while mounted, then unmounting and asserting no further revocation — or drop that clause from the name if the unmount assertion does not make sense.

For B and C, confirm each new assertion actually FAILS against the behaviour it claims to pin (e.g. temporarily loosen the code or the timer and check the test goes red). Report that you did this.

## Rules that will fail CI or review if broken
- NEVER apply a review suggestion literally — it is a symptom report, not a spec. Applying suggestions verbatim has twice caused a worse bug in this repo.
- Comments explain WHY, not what, and stay short. No comment defending an absent path or unchanged code. No tracker refs like `#1234` in code — `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` is a CI gate.
- Tests assert runtime behaviour, never source text.
- Prefer TS string literals over TypeScript enums.
- Do NOT flip the PR out of draft. Never run `gh pr ready`. Do not rebase or force-push.

## Gates — all must pass, run from inside the worktree
  pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  pnpm build
  pnpm typecheck
  pnpm lint
  pnpm lint:tracker-refs
  pnpm test
Note `apps/web` vitest only picks up `*.test.ts(x)` — a `.spec.ts` file is silently skipped, so name new tests `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx`.

## Then
1. Commit with a Conventional Commit subject, no parentheses in the subject line. End the body with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
2. `git push` to origin feat/bound-live-stream-tickets.
3. Reply to EACH of the 3 threads via:
   env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/1146/comments --field in_reply_to=<dbid> --raw-field body='...'
   saying what changed and where, or why you did not change it.
4. Resolve each thread:
   env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api graphql -f query='mutation { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "<id>"}) { thread { isResolved } } }'

Report back: your verdict on finding A with file:line evidence, what you changed for each of the 3, the gate exit codes, the new/changed test names, proof each new assertion fails without the fix, and the pushed commit sha.

A CodeRabbit verdict lands on one of **two** surfaces depending on the outcome, so polling only one
gives a wrong answer half the time. Observed across four PRs on 2026-08-04:

- **Clean** → `"No actionable comments were generated in the recent review. 🎉"` appears in the
  **issue status comment** (`issues/N/comments`), and `pulls/N/reviews` has **no** review with a
  non-empty body. Seen on #1036 and #1042.
- **Findings** → `"Actionable comments posted: N"` appears in a **submitted review body**
  (`pulls/N/reviews[].body`), and the status comment may never update. Seen on #1046 and #1049.

Polling only the status comment made a #1046 watcher report "still waiting" indefinitely while the
review had been sitting in the review body for 20+ minutes.

Two further traps:

- **Thread replies create `len=0` review events.** Counting `pulls/N/reviews | length` after an agent
  replies to and resolves threads shows several "reviews" that are not reviews. Filter to
  `select((.body|length)>0)` before concluding anything about rate-limit timing.
- A genuine review pass carries a **`Run ID`**, `Review profile`, and an `Estimated code review
  effort` line. Their absence means walkthrough-only or skipped, not reviewed — see
  [[project-coderabbit-walkthrough-vs-review-pass]].

**The login is `coderabbitai[bot]`, NOT `coderabbitai`.** On `issues/N/comments` the author login
carries the `[bot]` suffix, so `select(.user.login=="coderabbitai")` silently matches nothing and the
status-comment surface goes dark. Use `select(.user.login|startswith("coderabbitai"))`. This cost
hours on 2026-08-05: #1065 came back **clean**, the verdict went only to the status comment, the
poller could not see it, and three retries were spent "fixing" a review that had already happened.
(Note the opposite convention on GraphQL `reviewThreads`, where the author reads `coderabbitai` —
see [[project-greptile-second-pr-reviewer]]. The two APIs disagree; check each.)

**The status comment is MUTABLE and later requests overwrite the verdict.** Each
`@coderabbitai review` / `full review` edits the same comment in place, so a rate-limit notice
replaces the clean verdict that was there — destroying the evidence. Record the verdict when seen;
do not assume you can re-read it. Compare `created_at` vs `updated_at`.

**A stale body reads as a fresh verdict.** Fence on a timestamp captured at flip time
(`select(.submitted_at > $since)` / `.updated_at > $since`), or the poller re-reports the previous
review's findings as new — which happened on #1058, "finding" two issues already fixed.

**Incremental review refuses an already-touched SHA.** A walkthrough marks the commit reviewed even
when the review pass itself was fair-usage-gated, and every later ready-flip answers *"Already
reviewed. CodeRabbit is an incremental review system and does not re-review already reviewed
commits."* `@coderabbitai full review` is the documented override, but it still needs quota; when
depleted it replies *"Review rate limited … next included review available in N minutes"*, which is
the only unambiguous statement of the real constraint.

**How to apply:** poll `pulls/N/reviews[].body` (non-empty only) **and** the status comment filtered
with `startswith("coderabbitai")`, both fenced on a flip-time timestamp, matching either
`Actionable comments posted: [0-9]+` or `No actionable comments were generated`. Also: a script
gating on `gh pr checks` must distinguish a network error from a red check — an unreachable-API
error line counted as a failing check once caused a false ABORT that skipped a flip.

---
name: project-gh-needs-repo-flag-in-background-shells
description: "gh resolves the repo from the cwd, so a background poller without --repo returns EMPTY forever — always pass --repo FSM1/cipher-box"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

`gh pr view` / `gh pr checks` resolve the repository from the **cwd's git remote**. Outside a git
repo they fail with `failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository`, and with `--jq` that surfaces
as an **empty string**, not an error the caller notices.

Cost on 2026-08-08: two long-running CI watchers polled `gh pr view <PR> --json statusCheckRollup`
every 60 s for 45–60 minutes and logged `settled= pending= failed=` on **every** iteration. Both
reported "CI DID NOT SETTLE" while CI had in fact been green for most of that time. A `cd` to the
repo as the first line of the background command did **not** hold. Rate limits were untouched
(5000/5000), which ruled out throttling and pointed straight at the cwd.

Reproduce: `(cd /tmp && env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view 1145 --json mergeStateStatus)` fails.

**How to apply:** pass `--repo FSM1/cipher-box` on every `gh` call in any script, monitor, or
background task — it removes the cwd dependency entirely. `gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/...` is
already absolute and unaffected, which is why `recycle-both.sh`'s `gh api` polls kept working while
its sibling `gh pr view` calls went dark.

**Also treat an empty read as UNKNOWN, never as zero.** `pending=0` derived from a failed call looks
exactly like "nothing pending" and will score a red or unfinished PR as green — the same
false-all-clear shape as [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]]. Branch on `[ -z "$VAR" ]` first and
keep waiting.

Related: [[feedback_gh_auth]] (always `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`).

---
name: feedback-leave-pr-ready-after-clean-verdict
description: "Leave a PR READY after a clean or nitpick-only CodeRabbit verdict — re-drafting makes the merge-time flip burn a slot"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

When a CodeRabbit verdict comes back clean or nitpick-only and no further commit is needed, **leave
the PR in `ready`**. Do not re-draft it.

**Why:** the user stated it on 2026-08-08 — "this way a coderabbit slot is not mistakenly consumed on
a review that isn't necessary (when the pr is flipped to ready in the morning)". A draft→ready
transition starts a review, so re-drafting a clean PR means whoever merges it later pays a full
hourly slot for a review of a head that was already reviewed. With one review per hour org-wide
(see [[project-pr-reviewer-availability-aug-2026]]) that slot is the scarce resource.

**How to apply:**

- Clean or nitpick-only, no commit needed → leave READY.
- Actionable findings → re-draft **before** pushing the fix. A push onto a READY pr starts an
  incremental review and takes the slot the next pr in a chain is waiting for.
- Verdict never landed / unreadable → re-draft. That is the reversible side.
- To leave an already-drafted PR ready without burning a slot, flip it **after** another PR's flip
  has consumed the current hour. CodeRabbit answers with a rate-limit notice instead of a review and
  does not auto-retry, so the PR just sits ready.

Decide "clean" from the **inline comment count on the head**, not the review body text — a
nitpick-only review omits the `Actionable comments posted:` header entirely
([[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]).

Do not edit a cycle script while an instance of it is running; copy it and point the new run at the

When a CodeRabbit verdict comes back clean or nitpick-only and no further commit is needed, **leave
the PR in `ready`**. Do not re-draft it.

**Why:** the user stated it on 2026-08-08 — "this way a coderabbit slot is not mistakenly consumed on
a review that isn't necessary (when the pr is flipped to ready in the morning)". A draft→ready
transition starts a review, so re-drafting a clean PR means whoever merges it later pays a full
hourly slot for a review of a head that was already reviewed. With one review per hour org-wide
(see [[project-pr-reviewer-availability-aug-2026]]) that slot is the scarce resource.

**How to apply:**

- Clean or nitpick-only, no commit needed → leave READY.
- Actionable findings → re-draft **before** pushing the fix. A push onto a READY pr starts an
  incremental review and takes the slot the next pr in a chain is waiting for.
- Verdict never landed / unreadable → re-draft. That is the reversible side.
- To leave an already-drafted PR ready without burning a slot, flip it **after** another PR's flip
  has consumed the current hour. CodeRabbit answers with a rate-limit notice instead of a review and
  does not auto-retry, so the PR just sits ready.

Decide "clean" from the **inline comment count on the head**, not the review body text — a
nitpick-only review omits the `Actionable comments posted:` header entirely
([[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]).

Do not edit a cycle script while an instance of it is running; copy it and point the new run at the
copy. Editing a running bash script corrupted a run mid-flight on 2026-08-07.

_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**A failed `owe_retires` loses the reclaim debt permanently.**

`publish_node` at Line 1711 passes `Some(applied.op_id)` as `completes`, so the published-op mark is raised the moment the record acks. If `owe_retires` at Line 1726 then fails with a seam error, `publish_prune` returns `Err(Halt::Unclassified)` and the op stays queued, but the shortened history is already live. Two outcomes follow:

- The pass retries the op. `plan_prune` now sees the shortened history, `plan.retire_targets` is empty, and Line 1674 returns `Ok(())`. The dropped roots are never journaled.
- The device restarts. The published-op mark drops the op as already published, with the same result.

The dropped versions then stay pinned and charged to the account forever, and `pending_reclaim_bytes` never reports them. This is a leak rather than data loss, which matches the crate's stated preference, but the ledger is the only record of the debt and this path silently discards it.

Consider journaling the owed entries before the publish and treating a pre-publish ledger entry as advisory, or retrying `owe_retires` within the pass before returning.

Found the real cause, and it invalidates what I put in memory. **The inline background shell is zsh, not bash.** zsh does not word-split unquoted parameter expansions, so:

name: project-gh-needs-repo-flag-in-background-shells
description: "Inline Bash-tool commands run under ZSH — a multi-word command or flag held in a variable does not word-split, so `$GH pr view` silently returns nothing"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

**The Bash tool's inline commands run under `zsh`, not bash.** zsh does **not** word-split unquoted
parameter expansions, so the bash idiom of stashing a multi-word command or flag in a variable breaks
silently:

```sh
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"
$GH pr view 1146 --json statusCheckRollup     # zsh: command not found: env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh
R="--repo FSM1/cipher-box"
gh pr view 1146 $R --json ...                 # zsh: unknown flag: --repo FSM1/cipher-box
```

With `2>/dev/null` and `--jq`, both failures surface as an **empty string**, not an error — so a
poller reads "" and, if it treats empty as zero, scores a red or unfinished PR as green.

Cost on 2026-08-08: three CI watchers polled for 45–60 minutes each and logged `read FAILED` or
`settled= pending= failed=` on **every** iteration while CI had long been green. Diagnosed by running
the exact watcher line as a background probe: it printed `unknown flag` and `command not found`.

`recycle-both.sh` was immune all night because it is invoked as `bash script.sh` — inside a real bash
script the same idiom works. That contrast is the tell: if a snippet works in a `bash foo.sh` script
but returns nothing inline, suspect the shell, not the API.

**Wrong first diagnosis, recorded so it is not repeated:** the failure was initially blamed on
`gh` resolving the repo from the cwd, after a foreground `(cd /tmp && gh pr view ...)` failed with
`fatal: not a git repository`. That cwd failure is real but was a *different* failure reproduced by a
different command form, and `--repo` did not fix the watchers. Do not generalize a root cause from a
test whose command form differs from the failing one.

**How to apply in an inline Bash-tool command:**

- Write the command out in full — `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view 1146 --repo FSM1/cipher-box ...`.
- Or put the loop in a `.sh` file and run it with `bash file.sh`.
- Never store a command prefix or a multi-word flag in a variable inline.
- Treat an empty read as **unknown** and keep waiting; never as zero. Branch on `[ -z "$VAR" ]`
  first — the same false-all-clear shape as [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]].

Separately, `gh pr view`/`gh pr checks` do resolve the repo from the cwd and fail outside a git repo;
`gh api repos/OWNER/NAME/...` is absolute and unaffected. Passing `--repo FSM1/cipher-box` is still
worth doing, just not the fix for this bug.

Related: [[feedback_gh_auth]] (always `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`).

name: project-gh-needs-repo-flag-in-background-shells
description: "gh resolves the repo from the cwd, so a background poller without --repo returns EMPTY forever — always pass --repo FSM1/cipher-box"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2b9a962d-e9c8-4465-b4ef-93584f21a390

---

`gh pr view` / `gh pr checks` resolve the repository from the **cwd's git remote**. Outside a git
repo they fail with `failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository`, and with `--jq` that surfaces
as an **empty string**, not an error the caller notices.

Cost on 2026-08-08: two long-running CI watchers polled `gh pr view <PR> --json statusCheckRollup`
every 60 s for 45–60 minutes and logged `settled= pending= failed=` on **every** iteration. Both
reported "CI DID NOT SETTLE" while CI had in fact been green for most of that time. A `cd` to the
repo as the first line of the background command did **not** hold. Rate limits were untouched
(5000/5000), which ruled out throttling and pointed straight at the cwd.

Reproduce: `(cd /tmp && env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view 1145 --json mergeStateStatus)` fails.

**How to apply:** pass `--repo FSM1/cipher-box` on every `gh` call in any script, monitor, or
background task — it removes the cwd dependency entirely. `gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/...` is
already absolute and unaffected, which is why `recycle-both.sh`'s `gh api` polls kept working while
its sibling `gh pr view` calls went dark.

**Also treat an empty read as UNKNOWN, never as zero.** `pending=0` derived from a failed call looks
exactly like "nothing pending" and will score a red or unfinished PR as green — the same
false-all-clear shape as [[project-wave4-review-queue-state]]. Branch on `[ -z "$VAR" ]` first and
keep waiting.

Related: [[feedback_gh_auth]] (always `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN`).

content.content:
- name: Build packages
        run: pnpm --filter '!@cipherbox/web' --filter '!cipher-box' run build

  # The engine's browser artifact (blueprint/web-client.md "WASM packaging"),
  # built once per run. Every job that ships or exercises the browser engine
  # consumes this artifact, so a run's bundle and its e2e slice are the same
  # bytes by construction rather than by coincidence.
  wasm-engine:
    name: Web Engine WASM
    needs: [changes, lint]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.web == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.e2e == 'true')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # `target/release` is the host tree: under `--target wasm32-…` cargo puts
      # proc macros and build scripts there, so omitting it recompiles them on
      # every run. The native `target/<triple>` subtrees the cargo jobs cache
      # stay out — dead weight here, and a fourth full copy would push the
      # repo's other cargo caches out under LRU.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
--- Web Bundle job ---

  # The bundle that fingerprints the engine artifact. It consumes the module
  # `wasm-engine` produced, so it carries no Rust toolchain at all.
  #
  # Gated on `lint` rather than the usual `!failure()`: branch protection
  # requires this context by name, and a skipped required context counts as a
  # pass. So a failed `wasm-engine` must leave this job running and failing at
  # the download, not skipped and green.
  web-bundle:
    name: Web Bundle
    needs: [changes, lint, wasm-engine]
    if: |
      !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
      needs.changes.outputs.web == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
